issues.body:
### Context (where/what)

Add unit tests that exercise the Postfix log parsing code for three representative cases:

1. normal accepted/processed line (happy path),
2. SASL authentication failure line,
3. unexpected/garbled line that should be handled gracefully (no crash).
4. Create `tests/test_parser.py` and use small inline fixtures or files under `tests/fixtures/`.

### User goal

New contributors can safely change the parser with confidence. The tests document expected fields (timestamp, IP, username, event) and protect downstream outputs (CSV and email summary).

### Scope

- [x] Size XS/S (≤4h)
- [x] No breaking changes
- [x] Covered by 1 test or screenshot

### Suggested steps

1. Identify the parsing entry point/function(s) and expected output structure (dict/obj).
2. Create `tests/test_parser.py` with three parametrized test cases: happy path, SASL failure, unexpected format.
3. For the SASL case, use a realistic sample like `postfix/smtpd[1234]: warning: unknown[203.0.113.10]: SASL LOGIN authentication failed: authentication failure` and assert extracted fields (e.g., facility/component, IP, event type). 
4. For the unexpected line, assert the parser returns a safe fallback (e.g., None or {}) and does not raise.
5. Run locally with `pytest -q` and ensure CI stays green.

### Acceptance criteria (checklist)

- [ ] File `tests/test_parser.py` added, with ≥ 3 test cases (happy path, SASL failure, unexpected format).
- [ ] Assertions cover key fields (timestamp parsing, remote IP, event classification).
- [ ] Parser does not raise on unexpected/garbled input; behavior is explicitly asserted.
- [ ] Tests pass in CI (`pytest`) and use plain assert with clear failure messages (pytest assertion introspection).

### Code entry point

The parser function/module that reads and normalizes Postfix log lines (refer to the project’s parsing layer and where CSV/email summaries consume it).

### Skills

Python, Tests

### Ressources

- **pytest: writing assertions** - short official guide (use plain assert) [docs.pytest.org](https://docs.pytest.org/en/7.1.x/how-to/assert.html)
- **pytest: getting started** - how test discovery works (`test_*.py`) [docs.pytest.org](https://docs.pytest.org/en/7.1.x/getting-started.html)
- **Postfix SASL** - background on SASL auth and failure messages (useful to craft the sample line) [postfix.org](https://www.postfix.org/SASL_README.html)
- **Example SASL failure log lines** - real-world formats seen in maillogs [Server Fault](https://serverfault.com/questions/936269/log-username-in-maillogs-when-there-is-sasl-authentication-failure)

> [!NOTE]
> **Note to contributor**
>
> Keep test data minimal and realistic. If uncertain about expected fields or names, comment on this issue with your sample line and what you plan to assert; we’ll confirm quickly.

issues.title: Implement User Sign Up
issues.body:
**Description:**
This task involves creating the user interface for registration and the backend endpoint to handle creating a new user in the database. Security is paramount here.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1.  **Frontend:**
    * A "Sign Up" screen exists with input fields for `email` and `password`.
    * Basic client-side validation is present (e.g., checks for a valid email format and minimum password length).
2.  **Backend:**
    * A `POST /auth/signup` endpoint is created.
    * The endpoint validates incoming data (email is valid, password meets complexity rules).
    * It checks if a user with the given email already exists in the database.
    * The user's password must be securely **hashed** using `bcrypt` before being stored. **Plaintext passwords must not be stored.**
    * A new record is created in the `users` table.
3.  **Database:**
    * A `users` table schema is created. It should include at least `id` (UUID), `email` (unique), `password_hash` (string), and timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`).

**Technical Suggestions:**
* **Backend:** Use `class-validator` for request body validation. Use the `bcryptjs` library for hashing.
* **Frontend:** Manage form state using React hooks.

[devops] Dependabot Is not Updating Crates
issues.body:
## Description

Dependabot is failing to update Rust crate dependencies to their latest versions. This results in outdated packages being used in the project, which may miss out on important bug fixes, performance improvements, or security patches.

## Example

As of now, the latest version of the log crate is [`0.4.28`](https://github.com/rust-lang/log/blob/6e1735597bb21c5d979a077395df85e1d633e077/Cargo.toml#L4). However, our project is still using [`0.4.27`](https://github.com/nanvix/nanvix/blob/0a76c171254b505a07334dc6abd12661f324d7c6/Cargo.toml#L90), and Dependabot has not created a pull request to update it.


## Steps to Reproduce

- Check the current version of the log crate in the upstream repository.
- Compare it with the version specified in our Cargo.toml.
- Observe that Dependabot has not triggered an update.

## Expected Behavior

Dependabot should automatically detect and propose updates for outdated crates, including minor version bumps like `0.4.27` → `0.4.28`.

issues.title: [bug] Status component uses incorrect query param for session lookup
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The Status component in the client currently checks for an active session by filtering with the `macaddr` query parameter. However, the OpenWISP RADIUS API endpoint does not support filtering by `macaddr`; it expects `calling_station_id` as the query param for MAC address-based filtering.

**Relevant code:**
- [`client/components/status/status.js` (uses `macaddr` as query param)](https://github.com/openwisp/openwisp-wifi-login-pages/blob/e1ef7e0f7ad910faf51ff04c8ec878a865835e90/client/components/status/status.js#L217-L231)
- [The RADIUS API (`openwisp_radius/api/views.py`) expects `calling_station_id` for MAC address filtering.](https://github.com/openwisp/openwisp-radius/blob/4d9d85195624b60f157339e8884ac45539918f30/openwisp_radius/api/views.py#L808-L848)

**Steps To Reproduce**
1. Attempt to retrieve radius sessions for a user with a specific MAC address.
2. Observe that the frontend sends a `macaddr` query param to the API.
3. The API does not filter sessions as expected because it does not recognize `macaddr`.

**Expected behavior**
The frontend should use the `calling_station_id` query parameter when requesting sessions by MAC address, matching the OpenWISP RADIUS API's expectations.

issues.title: Optimize challenge cleanup in saveChallenge function using upsert pattern
issues.body:
## Description

The current implementation in `apps/kyc-server/src/lib/passkey/database.ts` uses a delete-then-insert pattern for handling WebAuthn challenges, which could be optimized using an upsert approach.

## Current Implementation

The `saveChallenge` function currently:
1. Deletes existing challenges for the identifier/rpId combination
2. Inserts a new challenge record

This approach performs unnecessary deletions even when no conflicts exist.

## Proposed Optimization

Replace the delete-then-insert pattern with an upsert using `onConflictDoUpdate`:

```typescript
// Current approach (inefficient)
await db
  .delete(challenges)
  .where(
    and(eq(challenges.identifier, identifier), eq(challenges.rpId, rpId)),
  )

await db.insert(challenges).values({
  userId: userId || null,
  identifier,
  rpId,
  challenge,
  expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000).toISOString(),
})

// Proposed approach (optimized)
await db.insert(challenges).values({
  userId: userId || null,
  identifier,
  rpId,
  challenge,
  expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000).toISOString(),
}).onConflictDoUpdate({
  target: [challenges.identifier, challenges.rpId],
  set: {
    challenge,
    expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000).toISOString(),
    userId: userId || null,
  },
})
```

## Benefits

- Reduces database operations from 2 to 1 in most cases
- Eliminates unnecessary deletions when no conflicts exist
- Maintains the same semantic behavior
- More atomic operation

## Context

- **File:** `apps/kyc-server/src/lib/passkey/database.ts`
- **Function:** `saveChallenge`
- **Lines:** Approximately 21-49
- **Related PR:** [#531](https://github.com/kindfi-org/kindfi/pull/531)
- **Comment:** [Discussion](https://github.com/kindfi-org/kindfi/pull/531#discussion_r2269106232)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Replace delete-then-insert with upsert pattern
- [ ] Ensure unique constraint exists on `identifier + rpId`
- [ ] Maintain existing behavior for `userId` handling
- [ ] Keep 5-minute expiration logic unchanged
- [ ] Add appropriate error handling
- [ ] Update tests if necessary

issues.title: Feature: Bitemporal Queries: Correctness, Pruning, and Snapshot Reproducibility
issues.body:
## Summary

Tighten semantics and performance for time-travel and valid-time queries. Specifically:

* Make `FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF …` and `VALID PERIOD [from,to)` **provably correct** against row version bounds.
* Add **temporal index pruning** and **predicate pushdown** so scans avoid non-overlapping versions.
* Introduce **snapshot tokens** to guarantee reproducible results for “as of TX/Timestamp” queries.
* Harden tuple (record) parsing around open/closed interval edges and null/±∞ bounds.

## Goals

* Correct evaluation of overlap between `(tx_from, tx_to]` and `(valid_from, valid_to]` vs. query cut(s).
* Optimizer can prune segments/rowgroups that cannot match temporal predicates.
* Stable **SnapshotHandle** (logical tx id + wallclock + epoch) that pins MVCC horizon.
* Clear rules for inclusivity: `FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF t` uses `tx_from ≤ t ≤ tx_to` (or `tx_to=∞`); `VALID PERIOD [a,b)` uses half-open.
* Observable speed-ups on temporal filters in `tests/` microbenchmarks.

## Non-Goals

* Full lineage GUI—CLI/SQL `lineage_explain()` only.
* Multi-shard causal snapshots (future work).

---

## Design

### 1) Canonical Temporal Overlap

Implement helpers (header-only `temporal.h`):

```cpp
struct Interval { Timestamp lo; Timestamp hi; enum Bound {Open, Closed}; Bound lo_b, hi_b; };
inline bool overlaps(const Interval& row, const Interval& q);
inline bool contains_point(const Interval& row, Timestamp t);
```

* Represent “infinite” as `kMaxTs` and `kMinTs`.
* Centralize inclusivity so executor and optimizer share logic.

### 2) Storage: Temporal Min/Max on Chunks

Augment row-page/columnar metadata with:

```
chunk.tx_min, chunk.tx_max
chunk.valid_min, chunk.valid_max
```

* Filled during append/compaction.
* Exposed to optimizer as **TemporalStats**.

### 3) Optimizer: Temporal Pruning & Pushdown

* Translate `FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF t` to `contains_point(tx_interval,t)`.
* Translate `VALID PERIOD [a,b)` to `overlaps(valid_interval,[a,b))`.
* Add a pruning rule: if `overlaps(chunk.interval, query.interval)==false` → skip.
* Push comparisons down to scan so the executor short-circuits early.

### 4) Snapshot Reproducibility

* Add `CREATE SNAPSHOT` (internal) generating `SnapshotHandle { lsn, clock_ts, epoch }`.
* `SET SNAPSHOT '<handle>'` pins MVCC visibility + disables “fuzzy” reads.
* `FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF TX <id>` resolved via handle→LSN table when available.

### 5) Edge-Case Parsing Hardening

* Normalize tuples with missing `*_to` to `∞`.
* Guarantee `from ≤ to` invariant; flip or error with diagnostics if violated.
* Unit tests for boundary conditions: exact equality on `lo/hi`, open vs closed.

### 6) Observability

* Tracing spans: `temporal.prune`, `temporal.overlap_check`, `snapshot.pin`.
* Metrics: `temporal_pruned_chunks_total`, `temporal_scan_rows_filtered_total`.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

* ✅ `FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF` and `VALID PERIOD` pass new spec tests for boundaries, null/∞, and equal endpoints.
* ✅ Temporal pruning reduces scanned chunks by ≥80% on synthetic skewed history (added benchmark).
* ✅ `SET SNAPSHOT` guarantees identical results across repeated runs while active.
* ✅ No regressions on non-temporal queries (CI).

---

## Tasks

### Engine / Executor

* [ ] Implement `Interval` + overlap/contain helpers.
* [ ] Wire helpers into scan node temporal predicate evaluation.

### Storage

* [ ] Persist `tx_min/max`, `valid_min/max` in chunk/segment metadata.
* [ ] Populate during append/compaction; backfill on load if absent.

### Optimizer

* [ ] Rule: derive temporal constraints from SQL → logical predicates.
* [ ] Rule: chunk pruning using `TemporalStats`.
* [ ] Pushdown: attach fast path to scan node.

### Snapshotting

* [ ] `SnapshotHandle` struct + serialization.
* [ ] `SET SNAPSHOT` / `RESET SNAPSHOT` plumbing to MVCC visibility.
* [ ] Map `AS OF TX` to handle when present; fall back to current mapping.

### Tests

* [ ] Unit: interval math (open/closed, ∞, equality).
* [ ] Integration: `FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF` & `VALID PERIOD` edge cases.
* [ ] Benchmark: history depth vs. pruned chunks and wall time.
* [ ] Fuzz: random intervals, ensure no mismatches vs. reference evaluator.

### Docs

* [ ] Update `README.md` (“Bitemporal Time Travel & Lineage”) with inclusivity table.
* [ ] Add `docs/temporal-semantic-tests.md` and optimizer note on pruning.

---

## Risks & Mitigations

* **Incorrect inclusivity semantics** → lock them in docs + golden tests.
* **Stats staleness** after compaction → rebuild on compaction; keep conservative.
* **Snapshot leaks** → RAII guard that auto-resets at transaction end.

issues.title: #1. Backend Setup
issues.body:
## Objective

Establish the foundational backend infrastructure for Stellarts, ensuring a scalable, maintainable, and production-ready codebase. The backend will serve as the API layer for artisan-client interactions, payments, authentication, and future feature extensions.

## Deliverables
## 1. Scaffold Backend Project Structure (FastAPI)

Create a new FastAPI project using a modular, clean architecture approach (e.g., app/ directory with submodules: `api/`, `db/`, `models/`, `schemas/`, `services/`, `core/`).

Implement a simple health check endpoint (`/health`) to confirm server readiness.

Include support for versioned APIs (e.g., `api/v1/`) to allow smooth upgrades later.

Add dependency injection pattern (using `Depends`) for database sessions and reusable utilities.


## 2. Set Up Environment Configuration

Configure `.env` file to store sensitive credentials (database URL, secret keys, API tokens).

Add a configuration loader (e.g., using `pydantic.BaseSettings`) in `core/config.py` to handle typed settings.

Provide a `.env.example` file with placeholder values for developers.

Ensure `.env` is excluded from version control via `.gitignore`.

## 3. Implement CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions / Docker)

Create a GitHub Actions workflow that:

Runs linting (e.g., `flake8` or `ruff`) and formatting checks (`black`).

Runs tests automatically on pull requests (`pytest`).

Builds the Docker image for the backend and runs it in a CI step to verify.

Set up branch protections so only code passing CI can be merged into `main`.

Document the CI/CD flow in `README.md` for contributors.

## 4. Containerization with Docker + docker-compose

* Write a Dockerfile for the FastAPI backend:

- Use a lightweight base (e.g., `python:3.11-slim`).

- Install dependencies from `requirements.txt` or `uv.lock`.

- Run the app with `uvicorn` (hot reload in dev, optimized in prod).

* Add a `docker-compose.yml` file to orchestrate:

- Backend API service.

- Database service (PostgreSQL).

* Provide make commands or shell scripts (`make up`, `make down`, `make test`) for easy local development.

## Success Criteria

* Developer can clone the repo, run `docker-compose up`, and access the `/health` endpoint successfully.

* CI pipeline automatically runs tests and linting on pull requests.

* Secrets are properly separated from code and securely managed via `.env`.

* Clear documentation in `README.md` allows a new contributor to set up the backend within 15 minutes.

issues.title: [!!!][FEATURE] Add PSR-14 Event before renderable is added to form
issues.body:
:information_source: View this commit [on Github](https://github.com/TYPO3/typo3/commit/e1871a14fb3eb5da281ad0c1fa949fd1d6d938e2)
:busts_in_silhouette: Authored by josuavogel j.vogel97@web.de
:heavy_check_mark: Merged by Oli Bartsch bo@cedev.de

## Commit message

[!!!][FEATURE] Add PSR-14 Event before renderable is added to form

A new PSR-14 event TYPO3\CMS\Form\Event\BeforeRenderableIsAddedToFormEvent
is introduced which serves as an improved replacement for the now
removed hook $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['SC_OPTIONS']['ext/form']
['initializeFormElement'].

The new event in comparison to the removed hook is dispatched
after the renderable has been initialized and right before
being added to its form.

Resolves: #107518
Releases: main
Change-Id: I0b7aea6a418541408965dfd997331aa736a5b9d0
Reviewed-on: https://review.typo3.org/c/Packages/TYPO3.CMS/+/90758
Tested-by: core-ci <typo3@b13.com>
Tested-by: Garvin Hicking <garvin@hick.ing>
Tested-by: Oli Bartsch <bo@cedev.de>
Reviewed-by: Oli Bartsch <bo@cedev.de>
Reviewed-by: Garvin Hicking <garvin@hick.ing>

## :heavy_plus_sign: Added files

<details>
<summary>14.0/Breaking-107518-RemovedInitializeFormElementHook.rst</summary>


```rst
.. include:: /Includes.rst.txt

.. _breaking-107518-1758539663:

========================================================
Breaking: #107518 - Removed "initializeFormElement" hook
========================================================

See :issue:`107518`

Description
===========

The hook :php:`$GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['SC_OPTIONS']['ext/form']['initializeFormElement']`
has been removed in favor of the more powerful PSR-14 :php:`TYPO3\CMS\Form\Event\BeforeRenderableIsAddedToFormEvent`.


Impact
======

Any hook implementation registered is not executed anymore in TYPO3 v14.0+.


Affected installations
======================

TYPO3 installations with custom extensions using this hook. The extensions
scanner reports any usage as weak match.


Migration
=========

The hook is removed without deprecation in order to allow extensions
to work with TYPO3 v13 (using the hook) and v14+ (using the new event)
when implementing the event as well without any further deprecations.
Use the :ref:`PSR-14 Event <feature-107518-1758539757>` to allow greater
influence in the functionality. Especially because the event is dispatched
later, it allows more modifications than the previous hook.

.. index:: Backend, ext:form, FullyScanned

```

</details>

<details>
<summary>14.0/Feature-107518-IntroducePSR14BeforeRenderableIsAddedToFormEvent.rst</summary>


```rst
.. include:: /Includes.rst.txt

.. _feature-107518-1758539757:

=========================================================================
Feature: #107518 - PSR-14 Event to modify form elements after being added
=========================================================================

See :issue:`107518`

Description
===========

A new PSR-14 event :php:`TYPO3\CMS\Form\Event\BeforeRenderableIsAddedToFormEvent`
has been introduced which serves as an imrpoved replacement for the now
:ref:`removed <breaking-107518-1758539663>` hook
:php:`$GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['SC_OPTIONS']['ext/form']['initializeFormElement']`.

The new event is dispatched right before a renderable has been constructed and
is added to the corresponding form. This therefore allows to fully customize
the renderbale after everything has been initialized.

The event provides the :php:`$renderable` public property.

Example
=======

An example event listener could look like:

..  code-block:: php

    use TYPO3\CMS\Form\Event\BeforeRenderableIsAddedToFormEvent;

    class MyEventListener {

        #[AsEventListener(
            identifier: 'my-extension/before-renderable-is-added-to-form-event',
        )]
        public function __invoke(BeforeRenderableIsAddedToFormEvent $event): void
        {
            $event->renderable->setLabel('foo');
        }
    }

Impact
======

With the new :php:`BeforeRenderableIsAddedToFormEvent`, it's now
possible to modify a renderable after it has been initialized and
right before being added to its form.

.. index:: Backend, ext:form

```

</details>

issues.title: Bug Report: VPC CNI IPv6 policy missing `ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute` permission
issues.body:
### Description
The VPC CNI IPv6 policy generated by the `iam-role-for-service-accounts-eks` module is missing the `ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute` permission, causing `MissingIAMPermissions` errors in aws-node pods when using IPv6 clusters.

### Affected Versions
- ✅ **Confirmed in v5.x** (tested with ~> 5.0)  
- ✅ **Confirmed in v6.0.0** (verified via source code)
- ❓ **Likely affects all versions** with IPv6 support

### Module Configuration
```hcl
module "vpc_cni_role" {
  source  = "terraform-aws-modules/iam/aws//modules/iam-role-for-service-accounts-eks"
  version = "~> 5.0"  # or 6.0.0

  role_name_prefix      = "vpc_cni"
  attach_vpc_cni_policy = true
  vpc_cni_enable_ipv6   = true  # This triggers the incomplete policy

  oidc_providers = {
    main = {
      provider_arn               = module.eks.oidc_provider_arn
      namespace_service_accounts = ["kube-system:aws-node"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Expected Behavior
The IPv6 VPC CNI policy should include all permissions required by [AWS VPC CNI documentation](https://github.com/aws/amazon-vpc-cni-k8s/blob/master/docs/iam-policy.md), including `ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute`.

### Actual Behavior

**IPv4/General Policy** (✅ correct):
```hcl
actions = [
  "ec2:DescribeTags",
  "ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces", 
  "ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes",
  "ec2:DescribeSubnets",
  "ec2:DetachNetworkInterface",
  "ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute",  # ✅ Present
  "ec2:UnassignPrivateIpAddresses"
]
```

**IPv6 Policy** (❌ incomplete):
```hcl
# Generated when vpc_cni_enable_ipv6 = true
actions = [
  "ec2:AssignIpv6Addresses",
  "ec2:DescribeInstances",
  "ec2:DescribeTags", 
  "ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces",
  "ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes",
  # ❌ MISSING: ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute
]
```

### Error Evidence
aws-node pods show this error:
```
Unauthorized operation: failed to call ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute due to missing permissions. 
Please refer https://github.com/aws/amazon-vpc-cni-k8s/blob/master/docs/iam-policy.md to attach relevant policy to IAM role
```

### Root Cause Analysis
According to [AWS VPC CNI IAM documentation](https://github.com/aws/amazon-vpc-cni-k8s/blob/master/docs/iam-policy.md), **both IPv4 and IPv6 modes** require `ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute`. However, the module's IPv6 policy block only includes a subset of permissions.

The issue is in `policies.tf` around line 160+ where the IPv6 dynamic statement is missing this permission.

### Proposed Solution
Add `ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute` to the IPv6 policy block:

```hcl
dynamic "statement" {
  for_each = var.vpc_cni_enable_ipv6 ? [1] : []

  content {
    sid = "IPV6"
    actions = [
      "ec2:AssignIpv6Addresses",
      "ec2:DescribeInstances",
      "ec2:DescribeTags",
      "ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces",
      "ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes",
      "ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute",  # ADD THIS
    ]
    resources = ["*"]
  }
}
```

### Current Workaround
Users must add an additional IAM policy:
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_policy" "vpc_cni_additional" {
  name_prefix = "vpc-cni-additional"
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect = "Allow"
      Action = ["ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute"]
      Resource = "*"
    }]
  })
}
```

### Environment
- **Terraform Version**: 1.13.3
- **AWS Provider**: 5.100.0  
- **EKS Cluster**: IPv6 enabled (`cluster_ip_family = "ipv6"`)
- **Tested and Verified**: Issue persists across v5.x and v6.0.0

issues.body: ``` dti = pd.date_range('2016-01-01', periods=5) dti.value_counts().index.freq # <-- None dti.factorize()[1].freq # <-- None mi = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays([dti, dti]) mi.levels[0].freq # <-- None ``` There is a comment in tests.indexes.datetimes.test_datetime `test_factorize` suggesting that freq should be preserved by factorize, but that is not checked and would fail if it were ``` # freq must be preserved idx3 = date_range("2000-01", periods=4, freq="M", tz="Asia/Tokyo") exp_arr = np.array([0, 1, 2, 3], dtype=np.intp) arr, idx = idx3.factorize() tm.assert_numpy_array_equal(arr, exp_arr) tm.assert_index_equal(idx, idx3) ``` So the question: do we want to try to preserve freq in factorize? xref #33677 for the MultiIndex case Update One more: Categorical: ``` dti = pd.date_range('2016-01-01', periods=5) cat = pd.Categorical(dti) cat.categories.freq # <-- None ```

issues.title: spss in search does not respect configured default
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The `max_spans_per_span_set: 0` configuration setting in the query-frontend is not respected when the `spss` parameter is not explicitly provided in search API requests. When no `spss` parameter is specified, the API automatically sets `SpansPerSpanSet = 3` (hardcoded default), which overrides the configuration setting and limits search results to 3 spans per span set.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
1. Start Tempo with configuration:
   ```yaml
   query_frontend:
     search:
       max_spans_per_span_set: 0
   ```
2. Perform a search request without the `spss` parameter:
   ```bash
   curl -G -s "http://localhost:3200/api/search" \
     --data-urlencode 'q={ status=error }'
   ```
3. Observe that only 3 spans are returned per span set, despite the configuration setting `max_spans_per_span_set: 0`

**Expected behaviour**
When `max_spans_per_span_set: 0` is configured, search requests without an explicit `spss` parameter should return all available spans per span set, not be limited to the hardcoded default of 3 spans.

**Environment:**
 - Infrastructure: [e.g., Kubernetes, bare-metal, laptop]
 - Deployment tool: [e.g., helm, jsonnet]

**Additional Context**
The issue occurs because the API layer in `pkg/api/http.go` sets a hardcoded default value of 3 for `SpansPerSpanSet` when no `spss` parameter is provided:

```go
req := &tempopb.SearchRequest{
    Tags:            map[string]string{},
    SpansPerSpanSet: defaultSpansPerSpanSet,  // Always 3
}
```

The `max_spans_per_span_set` configuration only affects frontend validation in `modules/frontend/search_sharder.go`, but doesn't influence the API default value. This creates a disconnect between the configuration intent and the actual behaviour.

**Workaround:**
Currently, users must explicitly specify a high `spss` value in their requests:
```bash
curl -G -s "http://localhost:3200/api/search" \
  --data-urlencode 'q={ status=error }' \
  --data-urlencode 'spss=10000'
```

**Related Files:**
- `pkg/api/http.go` (lines 121-124)
- `modules/frontend/search_sharder.go` (lines 100-102)
- `pkg/traceql/engine.go` (lines 102-107)

issues.title: [DOC] - How to Install MailLogSentinel on Debian 12
issues.body:
### Context (where/what)

Create a step-by-step guide for installing MailLogSentinel on Debian 13 (Trixie): prerequisites, installation, systemd setup (service and timer units), and basic verification steps (systemctl status, journalctl). The guide will be added to docs/install_debian13.md and referenced in the Quick Start section of the README. (Target audience: new contributors and users unfamiliar with the project)

### User goal

Reduce onboarding friction: enable anyone using Debian 13 to install, launch, and verify MailLogSentinel in ≤ 15 minutes, with a running service and a scheduled timer.

### Scope

- [x] Size XS/S (≤4h)
- [x] No breaking changes
- [x] Covered by 1 test or screenshot

### Suggested steps

1. **Prepare the environment**: update the system, install `Python 3`, `python3-venv`, and `pip`, create a virtual environment, and install the project dependencies.

2. **Install MailLogSentinel**: clone the repository (or use the archive), configure it minimally to read Postfix logs.

3. Create `systemd` units:

   * A `maillogsentinel.service` unit that runs the binary/script (within the virtual environment) as the appropriate user.

   * A `maillogsentinel.timer` unit (e.g., for hourly/daily execution, depending on the chosen frequency).

4. **Enable and start**: `sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now maillogsentinel.service maillogsentinel.timer`; verify with `systemctl status` and `journalctl -u maillogsentinel.service`.

5. **Document the Quick Start guide**: link to `docs/install_debian12.md` from the **README** and include a "Verification" section (expected log entries, where to find the CSV file/email).

### Acceptance criteria (checklist)

- [ ] The **docs/install_debian13.md** file has been created and is complete (including screenshots or command outputs).

- [ ] **README**: The **Quick Start** section has been updated with a link to this guide.

- [ ] `systemctl status maillogsentinel.service`: Screenshot or output showing the service as active (running) or that it was recently executed via a timer.

- [ ] **Copyable** verification commands (code block): `systemctl status`, `journalctl -u`, and `systemctl list-timers | grep maillogsentinel`.

- [ ] No changes to the application logic (documentation only + example `systemd` units).

### Code entry point

README (section Quick Start) et nouveau fichier docs/install_debian12.md. Exemple d’arbo pour les unités : deploy/systemd/maillogsentinel.service et deploy/systemd/maillogsentinel.timer

### Skills

Docs, Python

### Ressources

- [Debian 13 (Trixie) — Official Installation Guide
](https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/installmanual)
- [systemd Timers](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Systemd/Timers) (concepts and examples)
- [journalctl (man page)](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/journalctl.1.html) — checking systemd service logs

issues.body:
### Question

Hi,

I have a project which (transitively) depends on PySide6. Since the aarch64 build of PySide6 depends on manylinux_2_39 which is not satisfied for our use case, we decided to build our own wheels for the use case. I want to use `uv lock` to generate a lock file suitable for all the platforms (i.e. windows/amd64, linux/x86_64, linux/aarch64). Therefore I use

```
environments = [
    "sys_platform == 'win32' and implementation_name == 'cpython' and platform_machine == 'AMD64'",
    "sys_platform == 'linux' and implementation_name == 'cpython' and (platform_machine == 'x86_64' or platform_machine == 'aarch64')"
]
```

and I also played around with required-environments instead. Unfortunately, there seems to be no way to specify the python-platform (e.g. `aarch64-manylinux_2_35`) in these definitions, or at least I didn't find one.

The problem I'm facing is that I can't convince uv to use our self-build wheel for the linux aarch64 platform and the pypi wheels for all other platforms. I have tried to play around with

- index-strategy = "unsafe-best-match" (but it seems to either use pypi or the local wheel)
- required-environments
- platform-specific indices with marker = "platform_machine == 'aarch64'":

```
[tool.uv.sources]
pyside6 = [
    {index = "nexus", marker = "platform_machine == 'AMD64'"},
    {index = "flat-pyside6", marker = "platform_machine == 'aarch64'"},
]

[[tool.uv.index]]
name="flat-pyside6"
url="./path/to/pyside6-aarch64"
```

Are there any workarounds or suggestions for this use case?

issues.body:
## Description 📹

**Add network-level cron configuration to automatically refresh user configs**

Currently, the cron system only refreshes user configs based on the `refreshInCron` property defined at the starky module level. This issue proposes adding a network-level cron configuration that allows networks to specify whether their configs should be refreshed periodically, while still respecting the existing module-level refresh settings.

The enhancement would add a `cron` boolean property to network configurations in `configs/networks.json`. When set to `true`, user configs using that network would be refreshed during the cron job execution, but ONLY if the corresponding starky module also has `refreshInCron` set to `true`. This ensures both conditions must be met for automatic refresh to occur.

(Currently no configs have the cron enabled, but you can change that to do your tests)

issues.title: FSEvent.GetUuidForDevice is incorrect
issues.body:
The FSEvent.GetUuidForDevice has a few problems:

https://github.com/xamarin/xamarin-macios/blob/313bc16bc76b41b29b520c1d43af03c0ea9db8d5/src/CoreServices/FSEvents.cs#L94-L106

1. `FSEventsCopyUUIDForDevice` returns a retained object reference. This value isn't released (so it's leaked).
2. `FSEventsCopyUUIDForDevice ` returns an object reference. The code treats it like a blob of memory that contains the UUID. The fix is probably to call [`CFUUIDGetUUIDByte `](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corefoundation/1542119-cfuuidgetuuidbytes?language=objc) on the returned pointer.
3. No tests

issues.body:
## Overview

Implement the multi-step create project form within the `components/landing-page/project/CreateProjectModal` folder. This includes both the parent sheet and the `Contact.tsx` component. The form should follow the UI provided in Figma designs for both desktop and mobile, and include validation checks before moving between steps. 

 ### Follow the UI designs available here:

- **Desktop:** [Figma Design](https://www.figma.com/design/GxtSEhbK3VIkWoKwdgRdHi/Boundless?node-id=2839-34749&m=dev)
- **Mobile:** [Figma Design](https://www.figma.com/design/GxtSEhbK3VIkWoKwdgRdHi/Boundless?node-id=2943-64646&m=dev)

## Requirements

- Implement the multi-step form using the layout provided in the Figma prototypes.
- Ensure that form validations are in place and the user is prevented from moving to the next step unless the current inputs pass the validation checks.
- The implementation should reside in `components/landing-page/project/CreateProjectModal`, including relevant parent sheet and `Contact.tsx` component.

## Technical Considerations

- Follow the established coding conventions of the project (TypeScript, React/Next.js, and Tailwind CSS).
- Implement error handling gracefully, providing user feedback where fields are left empty or contain invalid data.
- Test the multi-step form thoroughly to ensure that validation rules block progression when applicable.

## Tasks

1. Review the Figma design prototypes (Desktop and Mobile) to understand the required UI components and form steps. 
2. Develop the multi-step form in `CreateProjectModal` ensuring that the parent sheet and `Contact.tsx` are updated accordingly.
3. Add client-side validation checks before allowing navigation to the next step. 
4. Implement appropriate error display for validation issues. 
5. Test the form across different devices to ensure responsiveness and proper validation behavior.

💡 **Note:** Ensure consistency with the overall design and user flow outlined in the [README](https://github.com/0xdevcollins/boundless?tab=readme-ov-file). 

## Definition of Done

- The multi-step form is implemented as per the Figma design for both desktop and mobile. 
- Validations are implemented and prevent users from progressing with invalid or empty entries. 
- The functionality is tested and verified in the designated components folder.
- Code follows the project's styling and testing guidelines.

issues.title: Registry: Clarify and document `registryType` possible values
issues.body:
## Description

In the context of [adding new entries to the Registry](https://opentelemetry.io/ecosystem/registry/adding/), we currently haven't documented the possible values and their definitions for the `registryType` attribute, which may cause contributors uncertainty when choosing the right value.

Page: https://opentelemetry.io/ecosystem/registry/adding/

----

> Is there an explanation of the registry types? I am getting confused on what the appropriate value should be here.

_Originally posted by @anders-swanson in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry.io/pull/7792#discussion_r2370321423_
       
----      

> Unfortunately no, but the rule of thumb is:
> - language: whatever language this application is written in
> - registryType, one of the following:
>   - "application integration" -> anything that is natively integrated, e.g. if Oracle DB would come with otel ootb, see https://opentelemetry.io/ecosystem/integrations/
>   - "core" -> otel core components, never applicable to non-project components
>   - "exporter": either an exporter component of the collector, or an exporter within a language-specific SDK, not applicable for a 3rd party component that is exporting telemetry
>   - "extension": collector or SDK extensions
>   - "instrumentation": instrumentation libraries or native instrumentations for libraries
>   - "log-bridge": implementation of log-bridges for languages
>   - "processor": collecor component "processor"
>   - "provider": collector compoent "provider"
>   - "receiver": collector component "receiver", not applicable for 3rd party components that are receiving otel telemetry
>   - "resource-detector": Resource Detectors for language specific SDKs
>   - "utilities": any other tool that people can use to work with OpenTelemetry, this is commonly used for components like what you have here.

issues.title: incident.io provider does not send deduplication_key on first firing, causing 422 error
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When using the native incident.io alert provider in Gatus, the first firing does not include a `deduplication_key` in the request body. As a result, incident.io responds with HTTP 422 ("Deduplication key is required") and no incident is created. This prevents incident.io integration from working out of the box.


### What do you see?

- Gatus triggers an alert for an endpoint configured with the incident.io provider.
- The POST request sent to incident.io does not include a `deduplication_key`.
- The incident.io API responds with a 422 error: "Deduplication key is required".
- No incident is created in incident.io.

### What do you expect to see?

- On the first firing, Gatus should generate and send a valid `deduplication_key` in the incident.io payload so that an incident is created.
- If `send-on-resolved` is enabled, the same key should be reused for resolve events.
- If not, a new key should be generated for each firing as needed.

### List the steps that must be taken to reproduce this issue

1. Configure Gatus with the incident.io alert provider:
   ```yaml
   alerting:
     incident-io:
       url: "https://api.incident.io/v2/alert_events/http/<id>"
       auth-token: "<token>"
   endpoints:
     - name: example
       url: "https://example.org/health"
       conditions:
         - "[STATUS] == 200"
       alerts:
         - type: incident-io
           description: "service down"
           send-on-resolved: true
   ```
2. Trigger an alert (e.g., stop the monitored service so that the endpoint fails).
3. Observe the outgoing POST request to incident.io and the 422 response.
4. Confirm that no incident appears in incident.io dashboard.



### Version

5.24.3

### Additional information

**Additional context**
- This happens because the provider only sets `deduplication_key` from `alert.ResolveKey`, which is empty on the first firing.
- See [alerting/provider/incidentio/incidentio.go](https://github.com/TwiN/gatus/blob/64a504365576cb8faa99a5242f9093783cb22591/alerting/provider/incidentio/incidentio.go) for reference.

issues.title: defaultProjectionData.fallbackMatrix and .mainMatrix do not reflect the correct types
issues.body:
I am currently in the process of making the MapLibre-project at my job functional in earlier browser versions. In our project we have a CustomLayer, in which I am passing the `defaultProjectionData` from its render-function to a glsl shader.

The `fallbackMatrix` and `mainMatrix` are typed as `mat4`, implying they are `Float32Array`, but in reality they are `Float64Array` being cast to `any` to circumvent the types of `gl-matrix` (see https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-js/issues/326#issuecomment-924249326).

Currently `gl.uniformMatrix4fv` accepts any `Iterable` returning numbers, but chrome <68 only accepted `Float32Array` or `Array<number>`, causing the CustomLayer to fail when trying to set the uniform.

as https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-js/issues/326#issuecomment-924249326 mentioned:

> It might be good to consider making a 64bit version/extend glmatrix to play better with Typescript for things like this..

which I agree with. It would be cool if `gl-matrix` had `mat<Float64Array>`! Else we could maybe add type annotations in the jsdoc?

The `fallbackMatrix` and `mainMatrix` are only 2 examples of this cast, it happens at multiple occasions throughout the codebase.

issues.title: Fragile String Comparison for Placeholder Automation
issues.body:
**File:** `ui/enhanced_main_window.py`
**Method:** `edit_automation`

#### Problem

Inside `edit_automation`, the placeholder is checked using a **raw string comparison**:

```python
if text == "[Enter automation script here]":
    return
```

This is fragile because:

* If the placeholder text changes even slightly (e.g., wording tweak, localization, spacing), the check breaks.
* It tightly couples logic to UI text, which should generally be avoided.

#### Impact

* Breaks easily during UI updates or translation.
* Inconsistent behavior if the placeholder is edited elsewhere but not updated here.
* Harder to maintain in the long term.

#### Suggested Fix

Use a more robust mechanism, such as:

1. **Store the placeholder text in a constant** so both the editor initialization and the check reference the same value.

```python
PLACEHOLDER_TEXT = "[Enter automation script here]"

# editor setup

self.editor.setPlainText(PLACEHOLDER\_TEXT)

# check

if text == PLACEHOLDER\_TEXT:
return

````

2. Alternatively, mark the editor with a **custom property/flag** to indicate “placeholder mode” instead of relying on string content.  
```python
self.editor.setProperty("is_placeholder", True)

if self.editor.property("is_placeholder"):
 return
````

#### Benefits

* Decouples UI text from business logic.
* Easier maintenance (UI text can change without breaking logic).
* Future-proof for localization or design tweaks.

**Description:**
This task connects the authentication system to the UI, ensuring that certain parts of the app are only accessible to logged-in users. It introduces the concept of protected routes.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1.  **Backend:**
    * A middleware is created to protect routes. It should check for a valid JWT in the `Authorization` header.
    * A new protected endpoint `GET /users/me` is created.
    * This endpoint uses the `userId` from the JWT to retrieve and return the logged-in user's data (for now, just their `id` and `email`).
2.  **Frontend:**
    * App navigation is structured to handle public (Login, Sign Up) and private (Profile) screens.
    * A "Profile" screen is created.
    * When the Profile screen loads, it makes an authenticated request to `GET /users/me`.
    * The user's email is displayed on the screen.
    * A "Logout" button is present. Clicking it clears the stored JWT and navigates the user back to the Login screen.

**Technical Suggestions:**
* **Backend:** This middleware is crucial. In Express, it would look something like `app.use('/api/v1', authMiddleware, protectedRoutes)`.
* **Frontend:** Use a library like **React Navigation** to manage the navigation stack and protect routes based on the authentication state.

issues.title: Accessibility Improvements (WCAG 2.1 Compliance)
Dark/Light Theme Toggle Implementation
issues.body:
## Description

Implement a theme switching system that allows users to toggle between dark and light modes. The theme preference should be persistent across browser sessions and provide smooth transitions between themes.

## What to Implement

- Theme context provider for global state management
- Theme toggle component in the header
- CSS variables and Tailwind configuration for themes
- LocalStorage persistence for user preference
- Smooth transitions between theme changes

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Toggle button switches between dark/light themes
- [ ] Theme preference persists across browser sessions
- [ ] Smooth animations during theme transitions
- [ ] All components support both themes consistently
- [ ] System theme detection (respects OS preference)
- [ ] Accessibility considerations for theme switching

## Technical Requirements

### Files to Create

1. **Theme Provider**
   - Path: `src/providers/theme.provider.tsx`
   - Purpose: Global theme state management

2. **Theme Hook**
   - Path: `src/hooks/useTheme.ts`
   - Purpose: Theme utilities and state access

3. **Theme Toggle Component**
   - Path: `src/components/ui/theme-toggle.tsx`
   - Purpose: UI component for theme switching

### Files to Modify

1. **Header Component**
   - Path: `src/components/layouts/header/Header.tsx`
   - Add theme toggle button

2. **Global Provider**
   - Path: `src/providers/global.provider.tsx`
   - Include theme provider

3. **CSS Globals**
   - Path: `src/app/globals.css`
   - Add CSS variables for themes

4. **Tailwind Config**
   - Path: `tailwind.config.ts`
   - Configure theme-aware classes

## Implementation Details

### Theme Provider Structure

```typescript
interface ThemeContextType {
  theme: 'light' | 'dark' | 'system';
  setTheme: (theme: 'light' | 'dark' | 'system') => void;
  resolvedTheme: 'light' | 'dark';
}
```

### CSS Variables Approach

```css
:root {
  --background: 255 255 255;
  --foreground: 0 0 0;
  /* Add all color variables */
}

[data-theme="dark"] {
  --background: 0 0 0;
  --foreground: 255 255 255;
  /* Dark theme overrides */
}
```

### LocalStorage Integration

- Store theme preference in localStorage
- Handle SSR hydration properly
- Fallback to system preference

## Design Considerations

- Theme toggle icon should indicate current state
- Smooth transitions (avoid flash on page load)
- Consistent color palette across both themes
- Maintain accessibility contrast ratios
- Consider reduced motion preferences

## Theme Colors to Define

### Light Theme
- Background colors (primary, secondary, tertiary)
- Text colors (primary, secondary, muted)
- Border colors
- Accent colors
- Status colors (success, warning, error)

### Dark Theme
- Corresponding dark variants
- Ensure proper contrast ratios
- Consider eye strain reduction

## Components to Update

All existing components should automatically support both themes through CSS variables:

- Cards and containers
- Buttons and interactive elements
- Tables and data displays
- Modals and overlays
- Navigation elements

## Accessibility Requirements

- Maintain WCAG contrast ratios in both themes
- Respect user's `prefers-color-scheme` setting
- Provide keyboard navigation for theme toggle
- Screen reader announcements for theme changes

## Dependencies

- React Context API (built-in)
- LocalStorage API
- CSS custom properties
- Tailwind CSS configuration

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Theme toggle works in header
- [ ] Preference persists across sessions
- [ ] All components render correctly in both themes
- [ ] Smooth transitions without flickering
- [ ] System theme detection works
- [ ] Accessibility requirements met
- [ ] No console errors or warnings

issues.title: [BUG] Resize request should throw 4xx as part of validation failure for write block
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Currently as part of the resize request validation while creating a target index using MetadataCreateIndexService, it throws IllegalStateException that gets translated to 5xx. Here it should instead throw IllegalArgumentException which will be translated to 4xx. 5xx is usually treated as server side failure/error whereas 4xx will be wrong user input which fits well in this case.

Ref: https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/blame/1a5331727b8037b4bcaf3e7c2a46dfb467259d13/server/src/main/java/org/opensearch/cluster/metadata/MetadataCreateIndexService.java#L1655

#### Response: 
```
HTTP/2 500 Internal Server Error
Date: Mon, 07 Jul 2025 15:48:17 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8
Content-Length: 315
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *

{"error":{"root_cause":[{"type":"illegal_state_exception","reason":"index test-01 must block write operations to resize index. use \"index.blocks.write=true\""}],"type":"illegal_state_exception","reason":"index test-01 must block write operations to resize index. use \"index.blocks.write=true\""},"status":500}
```

### Related component

_No response_

### To Reproduce

* Submit request to shrink an existing index (test-01) without write block on it.

```
curl localhost:9200/test-01/_shrink/test-shrink-01
```

### Expected behavior

OpenSearch should throw 4xx error instead of 5xx

### Additional Details
N/A

issues.title: STY: Enforce Ruff rule B905, zip-without-explicit-strict
issues.body:
`zip` calls should ideally specify `strict=True` since most of the time there's an underlying assumption that the input arguments are of equal length. To enforce this we should enable the Ruff rule zip-without-explicit-strict, https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/zip-without-explicit-strict/

Since there are about ~500 occurrences of `zip` in the code base, this issue should be completed in multiple PRs that adds `strict=True` to `zip` calls in a particular directory. Therefore, this issue can be worked on by multiple contributors.

For those interested in working on this issue:

1. Comment below on which directory you'll be working on. If you want to work on `pandas/core`, please choose a subdirectory in this location e.g. `pandas/core/internals`
2. Submit a PR adding `strict=True` (or `strict=False` if necessary) to `zip` calls

Once all `zip` calls are have a `strict` argument, a separate PR will be needed to move `"B905"` from the ignore section to the select section. https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/98c9c7f838d223e66f1459fab23ac178b29c2227/pyproject.toml#L395

issues.title: Set up NestJS Scaffold and Project Folder Structure
issues.body:
Initialize the SafeGig backend using NestJS with a modular folder structure that supports scalability, Postgres integration, and future smart contract interaction. This will serve as the foundation for all upcoming modules (Auth, Jobs, Escrow, Messaging, etc.).

Tasks:

Initialize NestJS project

Run nest new backend (or equivalent) with TypeScript.

Set up ESLint + Prettier for consistent code style.

Add .env.example for environment variables.

Install core dependencies

@nestjs/config for environment config.

@nestjs/typeorm + pg for Postgres integration.

@nestjs/axios for external requests.

cache-manager + @nestjs/cache-manager (for Redis later if needed).

@nestjs/passport, passport-jwt, jsonwebtoken for authentication.

ethers or viem for blockchain interactions.

class-validator + class-transformer for DTO validation.

Define base folder structure

```bash 
src/
├── modules/
│   ├── auth/
│   ├── jobs/
│   ├── escrow/
│   ├── messaging/
│   ├── users/
│   ├── notifications/
│   └── files/
├── common/        # shared decorators, interceptors, guards
├── config/        # env configs, DB configs
├── database/      # migrations & entities
├── utils/         # helpers (e.g. signature verification)
├── main.ts        # bootstrap
└── app.module.ts  # root module
```

Configure environment variables
Add .env.example with placeholders for:

DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:password@localhost:5432/safegig

JWT_SECRET=your-secret-key

BLOCKCHAIN_RPC=http://127.0.0.1:8545

Set up database connection

Configure TypeORM with Postgres.

Create a sample entity (e.g., User) + migration.

Verify DB connection works with npm run start:dev.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ NestJS project scaffold created and runs without errors.

✅ ESLint + Prettier enforce formatting rules.

✅ Environment variables load via @nestjs/config.

✅ Postgres connection is established and tested with a sample entity.

✅ Folder structure matches agreed modular layout.

issues.title: Tie validator onboarding secrets to a party hint and improve UI
issues.body:
Currently onboarding secrets work like this:

1. The SV generates a random secret. This is what is persisted on ledger in the onboarding contract as base64 encoding.
2. We base64 encode that together with the sv party id https://github.com/hyperledger-labs/splice/blob/4aa2cea6202f1d7ac6e773d89933489438d07f0b/apps/sv/src/main/scala/org/lfdecentralizedtrust/splice/sv/admin/http/HttpSvHandler.scala#L85. Note that this is not currently persisted. The sv party id never changes so we can generate it on the fly as needed.
3. This is then shared with the validator operator.
4. When the validator onboards we validate the SV party against the SV app and the secret against the on-ledger state.

The party hint is slightly different in that we need to persist it contrary to the sv party.

Concretely I would expect we can accomplish this by:

1. Extend the SV UI to specify a party hint when generating an onboarding secret.
2. When creating the on-ledger `ValidatorOnboarding` contract don't just include the random secret but include the full JSON object as a secret `{"sv": …, "validator_party_hint": "…", "secret": ""}` in the `candidateSecret` field of the contract (no Daml changes required that way).
3. When decoding, check if the first character is a `{` which must be the case for the JSON encoding and can never be the case for the old base64 encoding so we can be backwards compatible with existing secrets. If it is, decode it as json, otherwise decode it as the old format.
4. When decoding as the new format, validate the secret against the party hint in `/v0/onboard/validator`. If it mismatch, fail, otherwise continue.

In addition to that:
In the SV UI, provide a way to copy not just a secret but a text consisting of:

```
party hint: the hint
network: dev/test/mainnet
sv sponsor url: sv sponsor url they need to use in their onboarding
your secret: base64 encoded json secret
expiration: time with UTC offset
```

This can be used by the SV sponsor to copy directly into a slack message to send to the  validator they are trying to onboard.

issues.title: Incomplete Response Descriptions for Negative Offset and Limit Values in Organization Discovery GET API
issues.body:
**Describe the issue:**
When sending a GET request to the Organization Discovery API with negative values for `offset` and/or `limit`, the response descriptions do not clearly indicate which parameter is invalid. The error descriptions are generic and do not specify whether the issue is with the `offset`, `limit`, or both.

**How to reproduce:**

1. Negative Limit Value (limit < 0):

Request:
```
https://localhost:9443/t/carbon.super/api/server/v1/organizations/discovery?filter=&offset=10&limit=-1
```
Response:
```
{
    "code": "UE-10000",
    "message": "Invalid Request",
    "description": "must be greater than or equal to 0",
    "traceId": <Trace ID>
}
```

2. Negative Offset Value (offset < 0):

Request:
```
https://localhost:9443/t/carbon.super/api/server/v1/organizations/discovery?filter=&offset=-1&limit=1
```
Response:
```
{
    "code": "UE-10000",
    "message": "Invalid Request",
    "description": "must be greater than or equal to 0",
    "traceId": <Trace ID>
}
```

3. Negative Offset and Limit Values (offset < 0 and limit < 0):

Request:
```
https://localhost:9443/t/carbon.super/api/server/v1/organizations/discovery?filter=&offset=-1&limit=-1
```
Response:
```
{
    "code": "UE-10000",
    "message": "Invalid Request",
    "description": "must be greater than or equal to 0 must be greater than or equal to 0",
    "traceId": <Trace ID>
}
```

**Expected behavior:**
The error descriptions should clearly indicate which specific parameter(s) are invalid. The expected descriptions are as follows:

- For `limit < 0`: "limit must be greater than or equal to 0"
- For `offset < 0`: "offset must be greater than or equal to 0"
- For both `offset < 0 and limit < 0`: "offset must be greater than or equal to 0 and limit must be greater than or equal to 0"

issues.title: New feature: Support variable fonts
issues.body:
[Variable fonts](https://fonts.google.com/knowledge/introducing_type/introducing_variable_fonts) are a recent OpenType feature that pack multiple styles (e.g., weight, width, slant) into a single font file. Instead of requiring multiple `.ttf` files for each style (like `Roboto-Regular.ttf`, `Roboto-Bold.ttf`, etc.), one variable font can cover all variations.

This reduces the number of font files a user has to ship and gives more flexibility in adjusting styles dynamically.

Since **fontTools** is already a dependency of `fpdf2`, we could leverage its `varLib.mutator` to generate instances of variable fonts at runtime with custom axis values (e.g., weight and width).

Right now, you can load a variable font and patch it with `mutator` manually. See an example using [Roboto Variable](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto):

```python
from fpdf import FPDF
from fontTools.varLib import mutator

pdf = FPDF()
pdf.add_page()
pdf.add_font("Roboto-Variable", "", "Roboto-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf")
# default instance (wght=400, wdth=100)
pdf.add_font("Roboto-Variable-1", "", "Roboto-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf")
pdf.fonts["roboto-variable-1"].ttfont = mutator.instantiateVariableFont(
    pdf.fonts["roboto-variable-1"].ttfont, {"wght": 100, "wdth": 75}, inplace=True
)
pdf.add_font("Roboto-Variable-2", "", "Roboto-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf")
pdf.fonts["roboto-variable-2"].ttfont = mutator.instantiateVariableFont(
    pdf.fonts["roboto-variable-2"].ttfont, {"wght": 900, "wdth": 100}, inplace=True
)

pdf.set_font("Roboto-Variable", "", 20)
pdf.cell(w=pdf.epw, text="Roboto Variable Font - Normal (wght=400, wdth=100)", new_x="LMARGIN", new_y="NEXT")

pdf.set_font("Roboto-Variable-1", "", 20)
pdf.cell(w=pdf.epw, text="Roboto Variable Font - Thin (wght=100, wdth=75)", new_x="LMARGIN", new_y="NEXT")

pdf.set_font("Roboto-Variable-2", "", 20)
pdf.cell(w=pdf.epw, text="Roboto Variable Font - Thick (wght=700, wdth=100)", new_x="LMARGIN", new_y="NEXT")

pdf.output("variable_font.pdf")
```

**Proposed enhancement:**

* Extend `add_font` to optionally accept a dictionary of variation axes, e.g.:

```python
pdf.add_font(
    family="Roboto-Variable-Thin", 
    style="", 
    fname="Roboto-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf", 
    variations={"wght": 100, "wdth": 75}
)
```

* Or allow a mapping of styles to axis values:

```python
pdf.add_font(
    family="Roboto-Variable",
    style="",
    fname="Roboto-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf",
    variations={
        "": {"wght": 400, "wdth": 100},
        "B": {"wght": 700, "wdth": 100}
    }
)
```

* Add examples in the documentation.
* Provide test coverage

By implementing this feature you, as a benevolent [FLOSS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free/libre_and_open-source_software) developer, will provide access to the large community of fpdf2 users to a standard and useful PDF functionality.

Moreover, by working on this feature, you will learn about PDFs, fonts and the lifecycle & structure of a popular Python library.

You will also be added into the contributors list & map.

## Description
Implement an intelligent idle behavior for the Minecraft bot to mimic natural mob movement when not actively pursuing a specific task.

## Proposed Changes

1. **Feature Request**
   - Title: Implement Intelligent Idle Behavior for Minecraft Bot
   - Description: Develop a sophisticated idle behavior that includes awareness of surroundings and potential dangers.
   - Proposed Solution: Create an idle behavior module with random walking, danger avoidance, shelter-seeking, mob interaction, and periodic pausing.
   - Files to Modify: actions.js, skills.js, agent,js, etc...

## Files to Modify/Create
- `actions.js` (to implement new movement and interaction functions)
- `skills.js` (to create the idle behavior logic)
- `agent.js` (to decide when these behaviors should be used)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bot moves randomly when idle, covering an area of approximately 50x50 blocks
- [ ] Bot actively avoids stepping on or next to dangerous blocks
- [ ] Bot seeks nearest shelter when night falls or it starts raining
- [ ] Bot occasionally approaches and "inspects" nearby passive mobs
- [ ] Bot pauses movement at random intervals and rotates to look around
- [ ] Bot returns to designated "home" location after 5-10 minutes of wandering
- [ ] Idle behavior does not interfere with other active tasks or commands

## Additional Notes
This feature will make the bot appear more lifelike and provide a foundation for more complex behaviors in the future. Consider implementing a priority system so that the idle behavior can be interrupted by more important tasks, such as user requests for AI behavior.

issues.title: [feature request] Support various data segregation strategies in the State Management building block
issues.body:
We have data security requirements in our multi-tenant system whereby we need to :

1. Control how data is logically segregated by `tenant_id` when persisted.
2. Prevent developers from accidentally (or intentionally) omitting important query constraints that would restrict the result set to a given `tenant_id`.

Dapr State Management building blocks currently don't provide a way to achieve this dynamically at runtime for an unbounded amount of tenants, which makes it incredibly challenging, if not impossible, for us to adopt State Management in most of our use-cases.

However, if the State Management building block could become _tenant-aware_ and provide directives to the underlying components on _how_ to store/retrieve the data, that may enable us to utilise Dapr State Management.


## In what area(s)?

> /area runtime

### Checklist - [x] I have used the search function for [**OPEN**](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues) issues to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request. - [x] I have **also** used the search function for [**CLOSED**](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) issues to see if the feature was already implemented and is just waiting to be released, or if the feature was rejected. - [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible. - [x] This request contains only one single feature, **not** a list of multiple (related) features. ### App version 3.8.0 ### Feature or improvement you want | ℹ️ | **Implementation instructions**| |---|:---| | | This request has been discussed further below. If you're interested in implementing this, please see the [conclusions relevant for implementation below](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues/7773#issuecomment-3288670965).
The original post has been edited by the project maintainers to add this link. | Revise the 'Report bug' screen: * Add introductory paragraph (text tbc) * Add 'Report bug' button, which opens the URL to our forum in Bug category with pre-filled body text based on a) Environment information and b) Crash log * Change 'Open bug tracker' label to 'Open issue tracker on GitHub' * Alternatively, we can turn this also into a 'Report bug' button but specific to GitHub, again with pre-filled info, although I like the fact that we have a link to our general issue tracker (including feature requests) * Replace 'Copy to clipboard' button with a 'copy' icon on the text field itself * Add a 'trash' icon on the text field itself, in case a crash has been logged. Tapping it will remove the crash log data * Reduce the size of text buttons from full width to width needed to fit their contents ### Why should this be added? More prominently featuring our forum with a simple 'Call to action' will be a way out for frustrated users. This hopefully provides more actionable entry point than user sharing frustration in a Google Play review without any useful information ([example](https://play.google.com/console/developers/8008695526664634386/app/4974638472012894302/user-feedback/review-details?reviewId=4e97faec-c83f-4459-ad32-cfdc48d89653&corpus=PUBLIC_REVIEWS)). Most regular users will not know what GitHub is and don't want to create an account for it, leading them to the forum will provide a recognisable context. More advanced users who use GitHub will know where to tap. (Also, the button that opens GitHub currently has a wrong label, because it doesn't open only bugs.) I would like to have a 'clear crash log' button so I can remove the log after reporting an issue, so that I don't have to check the date of the crash log and think critically whether I have already reported it. ### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details How to create URLs that pre-fill posts: https://meta.discourse.org/t/creating-a-link-to-start-a-new-topic-with-pre-filled-information/28074 We might want/need to split the 'environment' block/field from the crash log block/field.

issues.title: [Task] Add unit test for VibeCheck class initialization with a dictionary config
issues.body:
**Task Description:**
Currently, we run unit tests using pytest which can be found [**here**](https://github.com/vibe-engineers/vibechecks/tree/main/tests). 

However, the test cases are not yet comprehensive enough and work can be done to cover more grounds. Specifically for this issue, we hope to add unit test for the `VibeCheck ` class.

The `VibeCheck` class can be initialized with a `dict` for the `config` argument. Add a new test case to `tests/test_vibecheck.py` that verifies this functionality. The test should create a `VibeCheck` instance with a dictionary as the `config` and assert that the `VibeLlmClient` is called with the correct `VibeCheckConfig` instance.

**Deliverable(s):**
New unit test that cover the testing of the `VibeCheck` class initialization with a dictionary config.

**Additional Context:**
- The `VibeCheck` class can be found [**here**](https://github.com/vibe-engineers/vibechecks/tree/main/src/vibechecks/vibecheck.py)
- You may refer to existing unit tests for the class as reference.

issues.title: ✨ Issue — Design Landing About in Figma ✨
issues.body:
## ✨ Issue — Design Landing About in Figma

## 📌 Description  
Design the **About section** for the Landing, scoped to `app/(landing)` only.  
Use the existing typography and color styles from the Figma file. Follow the reference layout (left copy block + right feature cards in a 2×2 grid).  

---

## 🧭 Scope  
- About section only: headline, body copy, single CTA, and 4 feature cards.  
- Desktop, tablet, and mobile variants.  
- Icons can be placeholders (consistent with Figma’s icon style).  

---

## 🎯 Goal  
A **handoff-ready About section in Figma**: responsive, well-balanced, with clear hierarchy and clean Auto Layout/constraints.  

---

## 🧱 Content (copy to use)  

**Heading:**  
*We Are Akkuea — The Future of Decentralized Education.*  

**Body text:**  
>Akkuea is a decentralized educational platform built on Stellar, designed to organize global knowledge with the power of AI and community collaboration. Our mission is to empower educators, reward contributions fairly, and give learners access to trusted, verified, and open resources.  

**CTA:**  
- *Learn More*  

**Feature cards (2×2 grid):**  
1. **Decentralized & Fair** — Powered by Stellar blockchain to ensure transparency, security, and fair rewards for educators.  
2. **AI-Powered Knowledge** — Intelligent indexing and personalized recommendations make learning efficient and accessible.  
3. **Global Access** — Breaking barriers: open resources for everyone, everywhere.  
4. **Community-Driven** — Learners, creators, and validators work together to build a collective future of education.  

---
## ✅ Figma Requirements  
- **Frames:**  
  - About — Desktop (1440)  
  - About — Tablet (1024)  
  - About — Mobile (375/390)  
- **Layout:**  
  - Desktop: two columns (left copy, right 2×2 cards).  
  - Tablet: cards stack in 2 columns below the copy.  
  - Mobile: vertical stack (copy → CTA → cards 1 column).  
- Apply Auto Layout, proper constraints, and grids for symmetry and spacing.  
- Build a **Card component** (title, description, icon slot); include hover/focus variants.  
- Reuse existing **Button** component style for the CTA.  
- **Accessibility:** readable line length, visible focus, min tap target 44px, consistent heading hierarchy.  
- Reuse **Text/Color styles** from the Figma library (do not introduce new tokens).

issues.body: ## Describe the bug When typing in the private chat input box or random chat input box on small devices (Android/iOS), the layout breaks when the keyboard appears. - The **navbar shifts upward** and hides the partner’s profile/typing status. - The **input box goes under the keyboard** instead of staying just above it. - Menu options become hidden as well. - When focusing on the input, a **Y-axis scroll line is created**, so users can scroll up to see the text being typed. issues.title: Improve ImageType Handling – Auto-Detect Instead of Manual Specification
issues.body:
Currently, the watermarkImage methods require users to manually specify the ImageType when processing an image. 

This is not ideal because:
- It forces users to know the image format in advance.
- It can lead to errors if the specified type doesn't match the actual image.
- It makes the API less intuitive for common use cases.

We should define the ImageType automatically and check during runtime if an ImageWriterSpi provider available for this image type to be able to perform ImageIO.write in the ImageConverter class.

More details about ImageWriterSpi here
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/59089118/javax-imageio-imageio-file-format-constants

NOTE: This issue is part of Contribute-to-Win. Please comment first to get assigned. Read the details [here](https://github.com/orgs/topoteretes/discussions/1361)

### Bug Description

This bug is encountered when using the cognee MCP server with http transport mode. Connecting to it through Cursor works without issue, however other agents and IDEs with agents have some trouble. 

I will use Cline in VSCode as the example. When trying to add an mcp server, all one needs in the json configuration in case of http transport is the url to which to connect. The configuration should look like so:
```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cognee": {
      "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```
What happens in Cline is the connection to the mcp server fails with a 400 error (Bad Request). 

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install VSCode and the Cline Extension.
2. Go to the settings for mcp servers in Cline, and put the configuration described above.
3. Run the cognee mcp server via a docker container (you can follow the instructions [here](https://docs.cognee.ai/cognee-mcp/mcp_quickstart))
4. When going back to VSCode and the Cline mcp settings, you should observe the 400 error.

### Expected Behavior

What is expected here is that Cline connects successfully to cognee mcp (an http 200 response), and it lists 11 available tools to use. It should be shown in green colour when it is successful.

Within the scope of this issue, this behavior is expected for all the IDE's that we have integration - refer to our [docs](https://docs.cognee.ai/cognee-mcp/mcp_overview) for all the tools need testing.

### Actual Behavior

There is a 400 error returned, and Cline cannot connect to the cognee mcp server. No tools are listed or available.

### Environment

- OS: macOS Sequoia 15.1, but it also happened on Ubuntu 22.04 Jammy
- Python: 3.11
- Cognee: 0.3.2
- LLM: All default ones
- Databases: All default ones

issues.title: [Good First Issue] [RISCV64]: Implement CPU plugin just-in-time emitter for SquaredDifference operation
issues.body:
### Context

[JIT Emitters](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/emitters/README.md) are part of code generation feature (a.k.a. tensor compiler) that automatically produces highly-efficient optimized fused subgraph binary code. Each emitter implements specific operation from low level OpenVINO dialect.

### Prerequisites
Due to limited resources, cross compilation is preferred option now for building OpenVINO targeting RISC-V development boards. Please see the documentation ["Cross compile OpenVINO™ Runtime for RISCV64 systems"](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/docs/dev/build_riscv64.md) for more details. For this work, you need to build [`xuantie-gnu-toolchain`](https://github.com/XUANTIE-RV/) or [`riscv-gnu-toolchain`](https://github.com/riscv-collab/riscv-gnu-toolchain.git) with `QEMU` support for emulation. So you don't need to have RISC-V development board even to contribute to OpenVINO for these platforms 😃 

### What needs to be done?

* Create `fp32` [SquaredDifference](https://docs.openvino.ai/2025/documentation/openvino-ir-format/operation-sets/operation-specs/arithmetic/squared-difference-1.html) operation [JIT Emitter](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/emitters/plugin/riscv64/jit_eltwise_emitters.hpp) for RISCV64 platform with RVV1.0 support. Use OpenVINO [CPU plugin JIT emitters](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/emitters/README.md) documentation and [RISC-V "V" Vector Extension](https://github.com/riscvarchive/riscv-v-spec/releases/tag/v1.0) documentation for details.
* Support your implemented JIT Emitter in the [JIT Executor](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/4ebe493140b90cbaaa68e2c71fe8e1dbd7461822/src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/nodes/eltwise.cpp#L805).
* Modify [RISCV64 kernel](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/4ebe493140b90cbaaa68e2c71fe8e1dbd7461822/src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/nodes/kernels/riscv64/jit_uni_eltwise_generic.hpp#L19) (in both places: [create_eltwise_emitter](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/4ebe493140b90cbaaa68e2c71fe8e1dbd7461822/src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/nodes/kernels/riscv64/jit_uni_eltwise_generic.cpp#L401) and [get_supported_precisions](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/4ebe493140b90cbaaa68e2c71fe8e1dbd7461822/src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/nodes/kernels/riscv64/jit_uni_eltwise_generic.cpp#L528)) to apply developed JIT emitter.

Before emitter implementation, please, modify tests to be sure that developed functionality is covered by test:
 * Add `jit` kernel check in [eltwise](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/0a177ff48a7197bee7eeb08f4e81b9d0ce8db271/src/plugins/intel_cpu/tests/functional/custom/single_layer_tests/classes/eltwise.cpp#L291) test, the test must fail.
* If test doesn't fail then add supported operation in [CPU eltwise test instantiation](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/0a177ff48a7197bee7eeb08f4e81b9d0ce8db271/src/plugins/intel_cpu/tests/functional/custom/single_layer_tests/classes/eltwise.cpp#L338) if it's absent.

### Tests
Tests are disabled in default build, so ensure to add `-DENABLE_TESTS=ON` into cmake command during the project configuration.

[GoogleTest](https://github.com/google/googletest) is used for testing. CPU functional test target is [ov_cpu_func_tests](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/tree/master/src/plugins/intel_cpu/tests/functional). You can use `GoogleTest` filter:
```sh
# If you use xuantie-gnu-toolchain:
<xuantie_install_path>/bin/qemu-riscv64 -cpu rv64,x-v=true,vext_spec=v1.0 ./bin/[platform]/[build_type]/ov_cpu_func_tests --gtest_filter="*smoke*Eltwise*SqDiff*"

# If you use riscv-gnu-toolchain:
<riscv_install_path>/bin/qemu-riscv64 -cpu rv64,v=true,vext_spec=v1.0 ./bin/[platform]/[build_type]/ov_cpu_func_tests --gtest_filter="*smoke*Eltwise*SqDiff*"
```

Description:

Right now Fuego emits an OpenAPI 3 spec at `/openapi.json`, but we are maintaining separately dedicated logic to handle REST calls on frontend.

This feature would let teams keep their backend and frontend in perfect sync.


### Issue:
- For frontend, we are currently manually writing API wrappers that duplicate backend definitions

- Reviewing and maintaining API client code is kind of an overhead


Solution:
- Already have open-api.json generated, see if we can use any codegen applications, to auto-genarate typescript API definitions and types so that we can directly use them as npm package.
- On every release, if there are any updates on specs, we can release corresponding package


You can check this OSS project, something i found when i was exploring: https://github.com/orval-labs/orval

Open to options here, you can explore and come up with better option from avialable libraries/tools.

issues.title: doc: Documentation issue in 'connectivity/bluetooth/api/l2cap'
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

There is insufficient information to create a working server example. (Not helped by there not being an example as well)

The following extract from the page: 
> Servers can be registered using [bt_l2cap_server_register()](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/doxygen/html/group__bt__l2cap.html#ga1a5e8c81c086872d7fb8da5329f982c6) API passing the [bt_l2cap_server](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/doxygen/html/structbt__l2cap__server.html) struct which informs what psm it should listen to, the required security level sec_level, and the callback accept which is called to authorize incoming connection requests and allocate channel instances.

There is a lack of information as to how to set the l2cap channel call backs, which can be set using the struct bt_l2cap_chan_ops, in order to receive data and also get events such as l2cap connect disconnect etc etc.
To do this:
1. create and set the accept call back when registering the server. 
2. create a bt_l2cap_le_chan instance with the chan.ops (struct bt_l2cap_chan_ops) set with the call backs you require
3. within the created accept call back set the bt_l2cap_chan to your instance

currently one of the best examples is in: zephyr\tests\bsim\bluetooth\host\l2cap\credits\src\main.c

### Regression

- [ ] This is a regression.

### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### Impact

Annoyance – Minor irritation; no significant impact on usability or functionality.

### Environment

- Page: connectivity/bluetooth/api/l2cap
- Version: main
- SHA-1: 12ddf997824605c17357aa88146bc4a8273c7968

### Additional Context

This issue was reported from the online documentation page using the 'Report an issue' button.

Changes we could make from this: * Clear any `__pycache__` directories. * Avoid shipping our own `.gitignore` * Update/remove our embedded jquery library. * Investigate why we create `opt/venvs/matrix-synapse/`, and if that is only for `.gitignore` (edit: related [matrix-synapse-py3.links](https://github.com/element-hq/synapse/blob/develop/debian/matrix-synapse-py3.links)) * Look into the `unusual-interpreter` errors. Do we need to be including these binaries? (Don't worry, `ckeygen` is [a unix tool for connecting to SSH servers](https://linux.die.net/man/1/ckeygen)). * The `uses-implicit-await-trigger` tag is a result of [this code](https://github.com/element-hq/synapse/blob/6ff181dbc7825f9dcb4eef0e6506b616b27a1d2f/debian/build_virtualenv#L126-L136) having a vague `interest` trigger, which defaults to `interest-await`. We should make it explicit by either specifying `interest-await` or `interest-noawait`, and justify the choice either way (`dh-virtualenv-interpreter-update` does not need await, so I would choose `interest-noawait`.)
