issues.title: Handle too big relayer log page size
issues.body:
## Overview

Some Ethereum RPC provides usually don't allow more than `10_000` events per response. Because of that, setting a big value for `--relayer-log-page-size` may lead to a stuck synchronization with L1.

We need to teach the Relayer service to adjust the page size. 

## Definition of done
When the RPC provider returns an error that the response is too big, we need to decrease the page size automatically.

If we decreased the page size, and for some period of time we didn't have any error, we should try to increase it.

The increased page size shouldn't be more than `--relayer-log-page-size`.

## Description

We would want to have a project, secrets, and variables to be automatically created for the default workspace. Currently, whenever a user signs up, they get a default workspace automatically created named **My Workspace**. We would want to extend this functionality.

Having a test project pre-created in the workspace would allow users to tinker around in the platform without adding any extra data.

issues.title: [asan] NPD calling prctl with PR_SET_VMA PR_SET_VMA_ANON_NAME and nullptr for name
issues.body:
```c++
unsigned long name = reinterpret_cast<unsigned long>(nullptr);
prctl(PR_SET_VMA, PR_SET_VMA_ANON_NAME, start, len, name);
```
will crash in `internal_strlen` called from the prctl asan interceptor.

`man 2 prctl` states:

> PR_SET_VMA (since Linux 5.17)
> PR_SET_VMA_ANON_NAME
> If arg5  is  NULL, the name of the appropriate anonymous virtual memory areas will be re‐set.

So it is valid and expected to be able to call `prctl` with the 5th parameter set to `NULL`.  It's UB to call `strlen` with `NULL`; and in this case, `internal_strlen` immediately dereferences the pointer it's given.

a4c97e1937997

cc @vitalybuka @eugenis @devnexen

issues.title: Addressing Memory Inefficient NR ray-surface intersection algorithm in the torch backend
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/HarrisonKramer/optiland/issues) and [discussions](https://github.com/HarrisonKramer/optiland/discussions) for a similar question or feature request.
- [x] I have read the [documentation](https://optiland.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) and tried to find an answer there.
- [x] I am using the **latest version** of Optiland.
- [x] I have included **all necessary context**.

*Thanks for taking the time to go through this — it really helps us help you!*

### Feature Request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The current implementation of the NR method to find the intersection of rays with surfaces works well. One of the nice things about Optiland is its dual backend architecture, which when using Pytorch, allows us to use the Differentiable Ray Tracing methodology for implementing optimization pipelines, etc. However, using a large number of rays, for a not so easy to define surface, like a freeform, the iterative NR is currently recording all the iterations steps in the computational graph in the forward path. This impacts the memory consumption very negatively. Therefore, it is a **must** that we somehow improve this method. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
As described in the paper "dO: A differentiable engine for Deep Lens design
 of computational imaging systems" (https://github.com/vccimaging/DiffOptics), there is a smarter way to implement the root solving method to find the intersection of the rays with the surfaces that is much more memory efficient. I would say we work out their logic, how exactly are they bypassing this problem while retaining the AD graph intact, and iterate from there - or simply implement their approach (with the correct copyright notice of course).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Since this is probably a major bottleneck in performance for Differentiable Ray Tracing, I am pretty confident that there are some people already working on smarter more efficient ways of finding the intersections of rays with surfaces, potentially speeding up the whole design optimization process in DRT pipelines. However, I am unaware of anyone working on it concretely. Maybe someone else out there would like to help us out implement some nice algos.

issues.title: Add GitHub Actions CI for backend (install, lint, build, test)
issues.body:
Summary

Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs CI for the backend: installs dependencies, runs linter, builds the project, and runs tests on a Node.js matrix. This will prevent regressions and ensure PRs have automated checks for build and test coverage.

What to add (files)

- `.github/workflows/backend-ci.yml` — workflow that runs on push and pull_request for `main` and other branches.

Suggested workflow behavior

- Runs on push and pull_request for `main` and feature branches.
- Matrix: Node.js 18 and 20 (adjust if project requires other versions).
- Steps:
  1. Checkout repo.
  2. Setup Node (matrix).
  3. Install dependencies with `npm ci` or `npm install` in `backend/`.
  4. Run linter if `lint` script exists: `npm run lint`.
  5. Build: `npm run build`.
  6. Run tests: `npm test` (or `npm run test`), and optionally upload test results/coverage as artifacts.
  7. Optional: cache node_modules / pnpm store to speed up CI.

Example minimal job summary (for reviewer)

- job: test
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  strategy:
    matrix:
      node-version: [18.x, 20.x]
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
    - name: Install deps
      run: npm ci
      working-directory: backend
    - name: Lint
      run: npm run lint --if-present
      working-directory: backend
    - name: Build
      run: npm run build
      working-directory: backend
    - name: Test
      run: npm test
      working-directory: backend

Acceptance criteria

- A new workflow file `.github/workflows/backend-ci.yml` exists and is syntactically valid.
- On PRs and pushes the workflow runs, installs dependencies, builds the backend and runs tests.
- The workflow marks the PR as failing if `npm run build` or `npm test` fails.
- The workflow is reasonably fast (uses caching where possible).

Verification steps for reviewer

1. Create a small branch with a trivial change (e.g. update README) and push a PR.
2. Ensure Actions runs and shows the `backend-ci` job.
3. Confirm the job completes the install, lint, build, and test steps; failures show clear logs.

Notes & edge-cases

- If tests require a running Postgres, either mock DB calls in unit tests or add a service container (Postgres) to the workflow and set `DATABASE_URL` in job env to point to the service.
- If the project uses a package manager other than npm (pnpm/yarn), adjust install step.
- If test scripts are missing or named differently, update the workflow to call the correct scripts.

Labels (suggested)

- ci
- enhancement
- good first issue

If you'd like, I can implement the workflow and open a PR with the file created and minimal caching. Reply "yes" to proceed and I'll add it and run basic validation.

issues.title: [FEATURE] : [SILVERFLOW] Add Integrity Check Support for Authorize, PSync, Refund and RSync Flows
issues.body:
### Feature Description/Summary

Integrity check is a scenario where there is a discrepancy between the amount sent in the request and the amount received from the connector, which is checked during response handling.

### Context
Integrity checks in a payments flow are critical for ensuring data consistency, correctness, and security when dealing with amounts between Hyperswitch and connectors like Adyen, Stripe, Razorpay, etc.

### Starter Tasks

- In the `handle_response` function of Authorize/PSync/Refund/RSync, you will have to call the respective functions - `get_authorise_integrity_object` for Authorize, `get_sync_integrity_object` for Payments Sync, `get_refund_integrity_object` for Refund and RSync and `get_capture_integrity_object` for Capture. 
- You would have to call these functions from `crates/hyperswitch_connectors/src/utils.rs`.
- These functions expect `amount_convertor`, `amount` and `currency`.
- You can take a look at this [PR](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/pull/8075) for reference.

### Implementation Hints

- You can go to `crates/hyperswitch_connectors/src/connectors/silverflow.rs` and call the respective integrity check function as stated above in the `handle_response` function

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Request and Response body added for each of the flows where integrity check is applied.
- [ ] All the required GitHub checks passing
- [ ] Formatted the code using `cargo +nightly fmt --all`

### How to Test it 

- Hardcode the amount or currency field that is being passed to the connector different from the one you are passing in the request body
- This way you would be able to reproduce the integrity checks error message while testing.

[Smithy Framework] - Extend our Smithy Framework to Payment Methods Update API and its corresponding Request/Response Payloads
issues.body:
## Summary

Extend our Smithy Framework to Payment Methods Update (/payment_methods/{payment_method_id}/update) POST API, an existing Hyperswitch API and its Request/Response Payloads.

## Type 

Feature

## Context  

### What is the Smithy Framework?

__Smithy__ is an Interface Definition Language (IDL) and set of tools created by Amazon for building APIs and SDKs. Think of it as a way to describe your API's structure, data types, and operations in a language-agnostic format, then automatically generate client SDKs, server stubs, documentation, and validation code for multiple programming languages.

### 1. __Rust-to-Smithy Code Generation Pipeline__

Instead of writing Smithy models manually, you've created a system that automatically generates them from your existing Rust code. This is brilliant because:

- You maintain your source of truth in Rust
- Smithy models are automatically kept in sync
- You can generate SDKs for other languages from your Rust types

### 2. __The Three-Crate Architecture__

__`smithy` crate__: Contains the `#[derive(SmithyModel)]` macro that you annotate your Rust structs/enums with.

__`smithy-core` crate__: Contains the core types and logic for:

- Representing Smithy models in Rust
- Converting Rust types to Smithy shapes
- Generating the actual Smithy IDL files

__`smithy-generator` crate__: A build-time tool that:

- Scans your entire workspace for types with `#[derive(SmithyModel)]`
- Collects all the generated models
- Outputs `.smithy` files

### 3. __How the Attribute System Works__

Your implementation requires the `#[smithy(value_type = "...")]` attribute on each field. This is crucial because:

- __Explicit Type Mapping__: Rust types don't always map 1:1 to Smithy types, so you specify exactly how each field should be represented
- __Field Filtering__: Fields without this attribute are ignored, giving you fine-grained control
- __Validation__: You can add constraints like `pattern`, `range`, `length`, etc.

Example usage from your codebase:

```rust
#[derive(SmithyModel)]
#[smithy(namespace = "com.hyperswitch.smithy.types")]
pub struct CustomerDetails {
    #[smithy(value_type = "String")]
    phone_country_code: String,
    
    #[smithy(value_type = "String")]
    email: String,
    
    #[smithy(value_type = "String", required)]
    id: String,
    
    // This field will be ignored in Smithy generation
    internal_field: HashMap<String, String>,
}
```

### 4. __The Generation Process__

I can see from your workspace that you have 65 structs/enums with `#[derive(SmithyModel)]` across various crates:

1. __Build Time__: The `build.rs` script scans your workspace for `#[derive(SmithyModel)]` annotations
2. __Model Collection__: Each annotated type generates a `SmithyModel` containing shapes, constraints, and metadata
3. __IDL Generation__: The generator creates `.smithy` files in the `smithy/models/` directory
4. __SDK Generation__: These `.smithy` files are then used with standard Smithy tooling to generate client SDKs



## Starter tasks

1. __Add the derive macro__ to your struct:

   ```rust
   #[derive(SmithyModel)]
   pub struct YourStruct {
       // fields here
   }
   ```

2. __Add the namespace attribute__ (choose one approach):

     ```rust
     #[derive(SmithyModel)]
     #[smithy(namespace = "com.hyperswitch.your.namespace")]
     pub struct YourStruct {
     ```

3. __Add `value_type` attributes to each field you want in the Smithy model__:

   ```rust
   #[derive(SmithyModel)]
   #[smithy(namespace = "com.hyperswitch.your.namespace")]
   pub struct YourStruct {
       #[smithy(value_type = "String")]
       pub name: String,
       
       #[smithy(value_type = "i64")]
       pub amount: i64,
       
       #[smithy(value_type = "Option<String>")]
       pub optional_field: Option<String>,
       
       // This field will be IGNORED (no smithy attribute)
       internal_field: HashMap<String, String>,
   }
   ```

4. __Add constraints__ (optional but recommended):

   ```rust
   #[derive(SmithyModel)]
   #[smithy(namespace = "com.hyperswitch.your.namespace")]
   pub struct YourStruct {
       #[smithy(value_type = "String", required)]
       pub id: String,
       
       #[smithy(value_type = "String", pattern = "^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$")]
       pub code: String,
       
       #[smithy(value_type = "i64", range = "1..=1000")]
       pub amount: i64,
       
       #[smithy(value_type = "String", length = "1..=255")]
       pub description: String,
   }
   ```

We are enhancing the Smithy framework by adding support for the Payment Methods Update API. This means annotating the request and response structs for this API with the Smithy macros so that the generator produces the corresponding .smithy models. This keeps our API definitions consistent, allows SDKs to include payment methods updation, and brings the Payment Methods Update flow in line with other APIs like Payments Create.
  

## Implementation hints

Refer to Payments Create API and its corresponding Request/Response Payloads, follow the same logic, how it is implemented for the API calls and how the Request/Response payloads are annotated for those APIs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All types and nested types present in Request/Response payloads must be annotated appropriately. 
- [ ] Run `cargo build` on the project to ensure that no compilation issue exists. 
- [ ] No change in existing business logic or functionality. 
- [ ] Run `smithy validate` to ensure that the Smithy Models generated from the annotated Rust structs are accurate. 


## Contribution Guidelines:

- Fork the repository and create a new branch for your work.
- Write clean, well-documented code with clear commit messages.
- Run formatter, and make sure that your code is properly formatted. 
- Make sure to follow our coding standards and contribution guidelines.

---

## Resources:

- Link to the Smithy Framework PR: [Smithy Framework PR](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/pull/9249)
- Link to the API endpoint specifications: [API Docs](https://api-reference.hyperswitch.io/introduction)

## Submission Process:

- Ask the maintainers for assignment of the issue, you can request for assignment by commenting on the issue itself.
- Once assigned, submit a pull request (PR).
- Maintainers will review and provide feedback, if any.
- Maintainers can unassign issues due to inactivity, [read more here](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/wiki/Hacktoberfest-Contribution-Rules).
- For this issue, please submit a PR on [@juspay/hyperswitch ](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch-web) repo, and link it to the issue.

issues.title: Make camera drivers to send their observations through shared memory
issues.body:
We have several camera drivers at `positronic/drivers/camera` directory. Currently all of them emit a dictionary of numpy arrays. 

In real life, the camera drivers live in the separate processes, hence we use multiprocess communication to send their data to the main processes (https://github.com/Positronic-Robotics/positronic/blob/main/pimm/world.py#L736)

Currently this data is sent over mp.Queue, which is essentially, socket-based communication, and the data get serialised and deserialised on both ends of communication channel.

In order to use shared memory for communication, one need to implement a `class NumpyDictAdapter(SMCompliant)` in `pimm/shared_memory.py` that would wrap such "dictionaries" into buffer and unwrap them back. You can use `NumpySMAdapter` as example.

issues.title: Add basic unit tests for `forklet.infrastructure.error_handler`
issues.body:
The error handling utilities (`error_handler`) provide decorators and exception classes to normalize errors across Forklet (e.g., API, network, authentication, rate limiting). Currently, this module has **no dedicated unit tests**.

We should add **simple and understandable unit tests** to validate the expected behaviors of exceptions and decorators.

---

### ✅ Expected Tests

1. **Custom exception classes**

   * Verify that `DownloadError`, `RateLimitError`, `AuthenticationError`, and `RepositoryNotFoundError` store and display the error message correctly.
   * Confirm that `DownloadError.__str__` includes the original error when provided.

2. **`handle_api_error` decorator**

   * Ensure that `GithubException` with status `403` and "rate limit" is converted into `RateLimitError`.
   * Ensure that `GithubException` with status `401` or `403` is converted into `AuthenticationError`.
   * Ensure that `GithubException` with status `404` is converted into `RepositoryNotFoundError`.
   * Ensure that other `GithubException` values are converted into a generic `DownloadError`.
   * Ensure that `httpx.RequestError` with "rate limit" or "429" raises `RateLimitError`.
   * Ensure that other `httpx.RequestError` values raise a `DownloadError`.
   * Ensure that unexpected exceptions are wrapped in `DownloadError`.

3. **`retry_on_error` decorator**

   * Verify that it retries the decorated function on `RateLimitError`, `httpx.RequestError`, and `ConnectionError`.
   * Ensure that it stops retrying after the maximum number of retries and raises the last exception.
   * Ensure that non-retryable exceptions (e.g., `ValueError`) are raised immediately.

---

### 📂 Suggested Location

Create a new test file:

```
tests/infrastructure/test_error_handler.py
```

issues.title: 🧹 Repository Cleanup: Remove Redundant Files and Improve Organization
issues.body:
# 🧹 Repository Cleanup: Remove Redundant Files and Improve Organization

## 🎯 **Objective**
Clean up the repository by removing redundant files, outdated documentation, and temporary artifacts to improve developer experience and reduce repository size.

## 📊 **Current State Analysis**

### **Repository Size Issues:**
- 50+ log files scattered throughout the repository
- 30+ temporary analysis documents in root and backend directories  
- Multiple redundant environment files
- Legacy documentation folder (`claudeDev_Docs/`)
- Cache directories and test artifacts tracked in git

### **Developer Experience Issues:**
- Confusing multiple `.env*` files
- Duplicate documentation in different locations
- Difficulty finding relevant information due to noise
- Slower repository cloning due to unnecessary files

## 🔍 **Files Identified for Removal**

### **🔧 Environment Files - REDUNDANT**
```bash
# KEEP:
env.example          # ✅ New comprehensive template (8KB, latest)
.env.ci             # ✅ CI-specific mock values (needed for CI)

# REMOVE:
env.dev.example     # ❌ Redundant (2.7KB, old format)
.env.dev            # ❌ Personal dev file (should be .env)
.env.example        # ❌ Old version (3.7KB, outdated)
```

**Rationale:** We now have the comprehensive `env.example` (8KB) that includes all settings. The `env.dev.example` is redundant and follows an outdated pattern.

### **📚 Documentation - OUTDATED**
```bash
# REMOVE ENTIRE FOLDER:
claudeDev_Docs/                    # ❌ Legacy Claude Dev documentation
├── claudeDevInstructions.md       
├── designDocumentSummary.md       
├── devNotes.md                    
├── ROADMAP.md                     
├── sprintDocs/                    
├── techStack.md                   
└── wireframes.csv                 

# REMOVE ROOT-LEVEL DOCS:
claudeDevInstructions.md          # ❌ Duplicate of claudeDev_Docs/
CLAUDE.md                         # ❌ Legacy Claude instructions
```

**Rationale:** The `docs/` folder is the official documentation structure. `claudeDev_Docs/` is legacy and outdated.

### **📊 Test Artifacts & Logs - TEMPORARY**
```bash
# LOG FILES (should be .gitignored but currently tracked):
*.log files (23+ files)           # ❌ Debug/investigation logs
*_output.log                      # ❌ Test output files  
*_results.log                     # ❌ Test result files
*investigation*.log               # ❌ Debug investigation files
*evidence*.log                    # ❌ Test evidence files

# CACHE DIRECTORIES:
.pytest_cache/                    # ❌ Test cache
.ruff_cache/                      # ❌ Linter cache  
.mypy_cache/                      # ❌ Type checker cache
__pycache__/                      # ❌ Python bytecode cache
coverage_report/                  # ❌ HTML coverage reports
test-reports/                     # ❌ Test report artifacts
```

### **📄 Temporary Documentation - ANALYSIS DOCS**
```bash
# ROOT LEVEL ANALYSIS DOCS:
CLI_TEST_OPTIMIZATION.md          # ❌ Temporary analysis
SERVICE_TEST_COVERAGE_ANALYSIS.md # ❌ Temporary analysis  
TDD_*.md                          # ❌ Development phase docs
issue_227_comprehensive_update.md # ❌ Issue-specific analysis
ci_pipeline_issue.md              # ❌ Issue-specific analysis
SEAMLESS_INTEGRATION_EPIC_*.md    # ❌ Epic planning docs

# BACKEND ANALYSIS DOCS:
backend/SETTINGS_MIGRATION_PLAN.md        # ❌ Migration planning
backend/TDD_RED_PHASE_*.md                # ❌ Development phase docs  
backend/TEST_*.md                         # ❌ Test analysis docs
backend/TOKEN_TRACKING_*.md               # ❌ Feature planning docs
backend/fixture_analysis_report.md       # ❌ Analysis report
backend/rag_quality_analysis_issue_227.md # ❌ Issue analysis
```

## ✅ **Files to KEEP**

### **🔧 Essential Environment Files**
- `env.example` - **NEW comprehensive template** (8KB, all features)
- `.env.ci` - **CI mock values** (needed for GitHub Actions)

### **📚 Official Documentation**
- `docs/` folder - **Official documentation structure**
- `README.md` - **Main project documentation**
- `CODE_QUALITY_GUIDE.md` - **Development standards**

### **⚙️ Configuration Files**
- All Docker, Make, pytest, and package config files
- `.gitignore`, `.dockerignore` files

## 🎯 **Implementation Plan**

### **Phase 1: Safe Removal (No Git History Impact)**
```bash
# Remove cache directories (not tracked by git)
rm -rf .pytest_cache/ .ruff_cache/ .mypy_cache/ __pycache__/
rm -rf coverage_report/ test-reports/ backend/test-reports/
rm -rf backend/.pytest_cache/ backend/.ruff_cache/ backend/__pycache__/

# Remove log files (should be gitignored anyway)
find . -name "*.log" -not -path "./node_modules/*" -not -path "./.venv/*" -delete
```

### **Phase 2: Git-Tracked File Removal**
```bash
# Remove redundant environment files
git rm env.dev.example .env.example

# Remove legacy documentation
git rm -r claudeDev_Docs/
git rm claudeDevInstructions.md CLAUDE.md

# Remove temporary analysis documents  
git rm CLI_TEST_OPTIMIZATION.md SERVICE_TEST_COVERAGE_ANALYSIS.md
git rm TDD_*.md issue_227_comprehensive_update.md ci_pipeline_issue.md
git rm SEAMLESS_INTEGRATION_EPIC_*.md

# Remove backend analysis documents
git rm backend/SETTINGS_MIGRATION_PLAN.md backend/TDD_RED_PHASE_*.md
git rm backend/TEST_*.md backend/TOKEN_TRACKING_*.md
git rm backend/fixture_analysis_report.md backend/rag_quality_analysis_issue_227.md
```

### **Phase 3: Update .gitignore**
```bash
# Add to .gitignore to prevent future accumulation:
echo "# Analysis and temporary documentation" >> .gitignore
echo "*_analysis*.md" >> .gitignore
echo "*_investigation*.log" >> .gitignore  
echo "*_evidence*.log" >> .gitignore
echo "TDD_*.md" >> .gitignore
echo "# Cache directories" >> .gitignore
echo ".pytest_cache/" >> .gitignore
echo ".ruff_cache/" >> .gitignore
echo ".mypy_cache/" >> .gitignore
```

## 📈 **Expected Benefits**

### **Repository Size Reduction:**
- **~50+ log files removed** (~10-20MB)
- **~30+ analysis documents removed** (~5-10MB)  
- **Cache directories cleaned** (~50-100MB)
- **Legacy documentation removed** (~2-5MB)
- **Total estimated reduction: 70-135MB**

### **Developer Experience:**
- ✅ **Cleaner repository** - easier navigation
- ✅ **Faster cloning** - smaller repo size
- ✅ **Clear documentation structure** - `docs/` is the single source
- ✅ **Reduced confusion** - no duplicate/outdated files
- ✅ **Better search results** - fewer irrelevant files

### **Maintenance Benefits:**
- ✅ **Single environment template** - `env.example` only
- ✅ **Consistent documentation** - `docs/` folder structure
- ✅ **Automated cleanup** - improved `.gitignore` rules

## 🚨 **Execution Strategy**

### **Recommended Approach:**
1. **Phase 1 First** - Remove untracked cache/temp files (safe)
2. **Create cleanup branch** - `git checkout -b cleanup/repository-maintenance`  
3. **Phase 2** - Remove git-tracked redundant files
4. **Phase 3** - Update `.gitignore` for future prevention
5. **Test thoroughly** - Ensure nothing breaks
6. **Create PR** - For team review before merging

### **Risk Mitigation:**
- ✅ **Backup branch created** before any changes
- ✅ **Incremental approach** - test each phase
- ✅ **Team review** - PR required for git-tracked file removal
- ✅ **Documentation preserved** - only removing duplicates/outdated content

## 🎯 **Success Criteria**

- [ ] Repository size reduced by at least 50MB
- [ ] Single environment template (`env.example`) only
- [ ] All documentation consolidated in `docs/` folder
- [ ] No log files or cache directories tracked in git
- [ ] `.gitignore` updated to prevent future accumulation
- [ ] All tests pass after cleanup
- [ ] Documentation links updated if needed

## 📋 **Acceptance Criteria**

- [ ] **Phase 1 Complete** - Cache and temp files removed
- [ ] **Phase 2 Complete** - Redundant git-tracked files removed
- [ ] **Phase 3 Complete** - `.gitignore` updated
- [ ] **Testing Complete** - All functionality verified
- [ ] **Documentation Updated** - Any broken links fixed
- [ ] **Team Approval** - PR reviewed and approved

## 🏷️ **Labels**
- `maintenance`
- `documentation`
- `cleanup`
- `good-first-issue`

## 👥 **Assignees**
- Repository maintainers
- Anyone interested in repository organization

---

**Note:** This cleanup will significantly improve the repository organization and developer experience while maintaining all essential functionality. The phased approach ensures minimal risk and maximum benefit.

The `RetryManager` is responsible for handling retries with exponential backoff when network operations fail. Currently, it does not have dedicated unit tests.

We should add **simple and understandable tests** to validate the following behaviors:

### ✅ Expected Tests

1. **Successful operation without retries**

   * Ensure that when the operation succeeds on the first try, no retries are performed.

2. **Retries on retryable exceptions**

   * Verify that `RetryManager` retries the configured number of times when `RequestException`, `Timeout`, or `ConnectionError` are raised.

3. **Stops retrying after max attempts**

   * Confirm that after the maximum number of retries, the last exception is raised.

4. **Non-retryable exception**

   * Ensure that if a non-retryable exception is raised, it is raised immediately without retrying.

5. **Exponential backoff delay calculation**

   * Test that the delay increases exponentially based on the backoff factor, and respects the `max_delay`.

```
tests/infrastructure/test_retry_manager.py

issues.title: 🧪 Tests: Add unit tests for `RateLimiter` (`forklet.infrastructure.rate_limiter`)
issues.body:
The `RateLimiter` is a **thread-safe mechanism** to control GitHub API requests, supporting:

* Primary rate limits (`X-RateLimit-*` headers)
* Secondary rate limits (via exponential backoff)
* Context manager usage (`with RateLimiter():`)

Currently, it does **not have dedicated unit tests**, which makes it harder to guarantee correctness and detect regressions in critical scenarios.

#### Proposal

Add a new test file:

```
tests/infrastructure/test_rate_limiter.py
```

Write **simple but comprehensive unit tests** for the following cases:

1. **Initialization & Reset**

   * Ensure `current_delay` is set to `initial_delay`.
   * Reset restores initial state.

2. **Update from headers**

   * `update_rate_limit_info()` correctly sets `limit`, `remaining`, and `reset_time`.
   * `is_exhausted` reflects remaining count.

3. **Wait behavior**

   * `_should_wait()` returns `True` when rate limit is exhausted.
   * `_calculate_wait_time()` respects exponential backoff.
   * Properly waits until reset when exhausted.

4. **Context manager**

   * Using `with RateLimiter():` updates `last_request_time`.
   * Delay resets on successful exit (`__exit__` with no exception).

5. **Thread safety**

   * Multiple threads can safely call `update_rate_limit_info` without race conditions.

#### Example (pseudo-code)

```python
def test_update_rate_limit_info_sets_values():
    rl = RateLimiter()
    headers = {
        "X-RateLimit-Limit": "100",
        "X-RateLimit-Remaining": "99",
        "X-RateLimit-Reset": str(int(time.time()) + 60)
    }
    rl.update_rate_limit_info(headers)
    assert rl.rate_limit_info.limit == 100
    assert rl.rate_limit_info.remaining == 99
    assert rl.rate_limit_info.is_exhausted is False
```

#### Benefits

* Increases confidence in API stability under rate-limiting conditions.
* Prevents regressions when optimizing backoff logic.
* Ensures safe usage in **multi-threaded** contexts (important for CI/CD pipelines with parallel jobs).

issues.title: Implement efficient sampling techniques
issues.body:
Sakana Labs recently released their paper on a similar implementation "ShinkaEvolve: Towards Open-Ended And Sample-Efficient Program Evolution" - https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19349

We can try and implement some of the ideas from that paper specially that help make the sampling of solutions efficient:

- Novelty rejection sampling: 

> Takeaways. Code embedding-based rejection sampling provides substantial performance gains over
> no rejection sampling by preventing redundant mutations. The additional LLM-as-a-novelty-judge
> offers marginal improvements, suggesting that embedding similarity is already an effective proxy for
> novelty assessment without requiring additional computational overhead.

- Bandit based LLM ensemble:

> Takeaways. The bandit-based LLM ensemble significantly outperforms both single LLM and fixed
> ensemble approaches. While the fixed ensemble shows moderate improvements over single LLM
> usage, the adaptive bandit strategy achieves the highest performance by dynamically prioritizing
> more effective models based on their contribution to fitness improvements.

issues.title: Feature Request: Emit `requestFinished` Event for Per-Request Bandwidth Tracking
issues.body:
Currently, the library emits a `connectionClosed` event, which is helpful for tracking the overall bandwidth usage of a socket connection. However, in many real-world scenarios involving persistent connections (e.g., HTTP keep-alive), it's valuable to monitor bandwidth usage on a **per-request** basis.

### Feature Request

I’d like to propose adding support for a new event, `requestFinished`, which would be emitted at the end of each individual HTTP/HTTPS request-response cycle.

While precise per-request bandwidth usage may not be trivial to isolate due to socket reuse, this event would still provide:

- A time-based approximation of bandwidth usage across requests.
- Insight into request frequency, response size patterns, and endpoint behavior.
- A hook for logging, monitoring, or quota management per request.

### Why This Matters

Tracking only at the socket level can obscure usage spikes or performance anomalies associated with individual requests—especially under connection pooling or when clients reuse a single proxy connection.

issues.title: Bug - providers.standard ExternalTaskSensor does not wait for external task to finish when deferrable=True
issues.body:
### Apache Airflow Provider(s)

standard

### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers

apache-airflow-providers-standard==1.1.0

### Apache Airflow version

2.10.5

### Operating System

debian

### Deployment

Astronomer

### Deployment details

_No response_

### What happened

When using the ExternalTaskSensor with deferrable=True:

If imported from airflow.sensors.external_task, the sensor behaves correctly by waiting until the external task completes.

However, if imported from airflow.providers.standard.sensors.external_task, the sensor incorrectly succeeds immediately, even though the external task is still running.

This results in premature success status for the providers.standard version of the sensor.

### What you think should happen instead

The sensor task should have waited until the task_id mentioned to it is completed

### How to reproduce

- Create the external DAG (sleep_dag):

```
from airflow import DAG
from airflow.operators.bash import BashOperator
from datetime import datetime

with DAG(
    dag_id='sleep_dag',
    start_date=datetime(2025, 5, 1),
    schedule_interval='*/5 * * * *',
    catchup=False,
) as dag:
    sleep_5_min = BashOperator(
        task_id='sleep_5_min',
        bash_command='sleep 300',  # Simulates a long-running task
    )

```
- Create the DAG using two ExternalTaskSensor variants:

```
from airflow import DAG
from airflow.sensors.external_task import ExternalTaskSensor as CoreSensor
from airflow.providers.standard.sensors.external_task import ExternalTaskSensor as ProviderSensor
from datetime import datetime

with DAG(
    dag_id='sensor_dag',
    start_date=datetime(2025, 5, 1),
    schedule_interval='*/5 * * * *',
    catchup=False,
) as dag:

    # Core Sensor (works correctly)
    core_sensor = CoreSensor(
        task_id='core_external_task_sensor',
        external_dag_id='sleep_dag',
        external_task_id='sleep_5_min',
        deferrable=True,
        timeout=600,
        poke_interval=30,
    )

    # Provider Sensor (succeeds prematurely)
    provider_sensor = ProviderSensor(
        task_id='provider_external_task_sensor',
        external_dag_id='sleep_dag',
        external_task_id='sleep_5_min',
        deferrable=True,
        timeout=600,
        poke_interval=30,
    )

```

- Trigger both DAGs and observe behavior:

The core_external_task_sensor waits for sleep_5_min to complete (correct).

The provider_external_task_sensor is marked as successful before sleep_5_min completes (incorrect).




### Anything else

**Olá dev.**

Para mais um tipo de contribuição, venho indicar uma nova característica que pode ser incrementado no projeto da **Calculadora Tk**, então segue abaixo:

***Que tal criar novos temas para a calculadora?***

Dentro do diretório [app/settings](https://github.com/matheusfelipeog/calculadora-tk/blob/master/app/settings) existe um arquivo [settings.json](https://github.com/matheusfelipeog/calculadora-tk/blob/master/app/settings/settings.json), nesse arquivo você criará seus próprios temas para a calculadora. Para isso, basta criar novos objetos json seguindo o padrão da já existente estrutura (não modifique ou apague temas, somente copie e adicione novos no arquivo com suas configurações), assim colocando suas próprias configurações que julga interessante para ter no visual da calculadora.

 **Estilos atuais:**
- [x] Dark;
- [x] White;
- [x] Estilo padrão para macOS.
- [x] Dracula
- [x] Dark Blue
- [x] Purple
- [x] Ocean 
...
- [ ] New ?

> Caso você não seja bom em escolher cores e criar uma paleta legal, deixo como dica a utilização do [Flat UI Colors](https://flatuicolors.com/) para consultar cores legais. 😁👍

issues.title: Support parsing Doris sql
issues.body:
## Background

Hi community.\
The ShardingSphere SQL parser engine helps users to parse SQL to create the AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) and visit the AST to get SQLStatement (Java Object). Currently, we are planning to enhance the support for Doris SQL parsing in ShardingSphere.

More details:
<https://shardingsphere.apache.org/document/current/en/reference/sharding/parse/>  


## Issue Background Explanation

The current issue involves using a custom web scraping script to fetch SQL cases from the official website of a corresponding database. These SQL cases are then passed to ShardingSphere's parsing engine for analysis. For SQL cases that fail to be parsed successfully, every 3 to 5 SQL cases are grouped together as an issue.
1. Since  SQL cases are obtained through web scraping, it cannot be guaranteed that all SQL cases are correct. Please follow the following process to handle this pull request (PR).
2. Some SQL cases may have already been fixed in other PRs. For cases that can already be executed successfully, simply leave a comment to ignore them.
3. If a SQL case can be executed successfully without any code changes, there is no need to add a corresponding test assert file.  


## Task

This issue is to support more Doris sql parsing, as follows:

```
BITXOR
```

- [ ] [link](https://doris.apache.org/docs/2.0/sql-manual/sql-functions/bitwise-functions/bitxor/)

```
BIGINT size(ARRAY<T> arr) BIGINT array_size(ARRAY<T> arr) BIGINT cardinality(ARRAY<T> arr)
```

- [ ] [link](https://doris.apache.org/zh-CN/docs/dev/sql-manual/sql-functions/array-functions/array-size/)

```
MySQL [(none)]> select starts_with("hello world","hello")
```

- [ ] [link](https://doris.apache.org/docs/dev/sql-manual/sql-functions/string-functions/starts-with/)

```
BITMAP
```

- [ ] [link](https://doris.apache.org/zh-CN/docs/dev/sql-manual/sql-types/Data-Types/BITMAP/)

```
BITAND
```

- [ ] [link](https://doris.apache.org/zh-CN/docs/2.0/sql-manual/sql-functions/bitwise-functions/bitand/)

```
CREATE TABLE test_show_data_skew (   id int,   name string,   pdate date ) PARTITION BY RANGE(pdate) (   FROM ("2023-04-16") TO ("2023-04-20") INTERVAL 1 DAY ) DISTRIBUTED BY HASH(id) BUCKETS 5 PROPERTIES (   "replication_num" = "1" )
```

- [ ] [link](https://doris.apache.org/zh-CN/docs/dev/sql-manual/sql-statements/Show-Statements/SHOW-DATA-SKEW/)

```
CREATE TABLE test_show_data_skew2 (     id int,     name string,     pdate date ) DISTRIBUTED BY HASH(id) BUCKETS 5 PROPERTIES (     "replication_num" = "1" )
```

- [ ] [link](https://doris.apache.org/zh-CN/docs/dev/sql-manual/sql-statements/Show-Statements/SHOW-DATA-SKEW/)

```
UCASE
```

- [ ] [link](https://doris.apache.org/zh-CN/docs/sql-manual/sql-functions/string-functions/ucase/)

```
ALTER SYSTEM ADD FOLLOWER "follower_host:edit_log_port"
```

- [ ] [link](https://doris.apache.org/zh-CN/docs/2.0/sql-manual/sql-reference/Cluster-Management-Statements/ALTER-SYSTEM-ADD-FOLLOWER/)

```
ALTER SYSTEM ADD FOLLOWER "host_ip:9010"
```

- [ ] [link](https://doris.apache.org/zh-CN/docs/2.0/sql-manual/sql-reference/Cluster-Management-Statements/ALTER-SYSTEM-ADD-FOLLOWER/)




## Overall Procedure

If you intend to participate in fixing this issue, please feel free to leave a comment below the issue. Community members will assign the issue accordingly.  

><u>For example, you can leave a comment like this: "Hi, please assign this issue to me. Thank you!"</u>

Once you have claimed the issue, please review the syntax of the SQL on the official website of the corresponding database. Execute the SQL on the respective database to ensure the correctness of the SQL syntax.

><u>You can check the corresponding source of each SQL case on the official database website by clicking on the link provided below each case.</u> 

Next, execute the problematic SQL cases mentioned above in the database (you can quickly start the                     corresponding database using the Docker image for that database, and then connect to it using 
a client you are  familiar with), to ensure that the SQL syntax itself is correct.  

## Fixing ANTLR Grammar Parsing Issue

Once you have confirmed the correctness of the SQL syntax, you can validate and fix the grammar parsing issue in ShardingSphere. 

>If you are using IntelliJ IDEA, you will need to install the ANTLR plugin before proceeding.

If it is an ANTLR parsing error message, try to repair the `.g4` file by comparing it with the official database syntax until the SQL can be correctly parsed by ANTLR.

When there is no error message in the ANTLR Preview window, it means that ANTLR can correctly parse the SQL.  

## Visitor problem fix

After ANTLR parses SQL into an abstract syntax tree, ShardingSphere will access the abstract syntax tree through Visitor and extract the required information.
If you need to extract Segments, you need to first execute:
 ```
 mvn -T 2C clean install -DskipTests
 ```  
 Under the shardingsphere-parser module to compile the entire parser module.\
Then rewrite the corresponding visit method in SQLStatementVisitorr as needed to extract the corresponding Segment.

## Add assertion test file  

After the above SQL parsing problem is repaired, the corresponding Test needs to be added. 
The steps are as follows:
1. Add the corresponding `sql-case` in the `sql/supported` directory.
2. Add case assertions in the case directory of the `shardingsphere-test-it-parser` module.
3.  Run `org.apache.shardingsphere.test.it.sql.parser.internal.InternalSQLParserIT`\
 After SQL Parser IT runs successfully, you can submit a PR.   

## Relevant Skills

1. Master JAVA language
2. Have a basic understanding of Antlr g4 file
3. Be familiar with Doris SQLs

issues.title: [Enhancement] Add Command-Line Arguments to Benchmark Scripts
issues.body:
## Description

Currently, `benchmark.py` and `multi_agent_benchmark.py` have hardcoded simulation lengths (e.g., `NUM_WEEKS = 52`). To make them more flexible for testing, we should allow these values to be set via command-line arguments.

## Steps
- [ ] Add Python's built-in `argparse` library to `tests/benchmark.py`.
- [ ] Define a command-line argument, e.g., `--weeks`, that allows a user to specify the number of weeks for the simulation.
- [ ] Replace the hardcoded `NUM_WEEKS_TO_SIMULATE` constant with the value from the command-line argument.
- [ ] Repeat the same process for `tests/multi_agent_benchmark.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A user can run `python3 -m tests.benchmark --weeks 20` to run a 20-week simulation.
- [ ] If no argument is provided, the script should default to 52 weeks.
- [ ] The script provides a `--help` message explaining the available arguments.

## References
- `tests/benchmark.py`
- `tests/multi_agent_benchmark.py`
- [Python `argparse` tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/howto/argparse.html)

The server crashes with an unhandled database error when a client tries to delete a notification that has already been deleted or no longer exists. This makes the entire server unreachable until it is manually restarted.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1.  Go to the Drop client application.
2.  Perform an action that creates and then deletes a notification in quick succession, or have two clients interact with the same notification.
3.  This triggers an API call to the server to delete a notification record.
4.  See the server crash and become unresponsive. The container will have an "Exited" status.

**Expected behavior**
The server should handle the error gracefully. If a request is made to delete a notification that doesn't exist, the server should simply ignore it or return a `404 Not Found` error without crashing the application.

issues.title: Replace shell script with Python
issues.body:
The current [shell script implementation](https://github.com/adfinis/vault-raft-backup-agent/blob/master/kubernetes/vault-snapshot.sh) for the Kubernetes CronJob works for simple scripting purposes, but does not scale well for more complex logic (such as custom retention and maybe other features in the future).

issues.title: Support properties `hibernate.type.preferred_*_jdbc_type`
issues.body:
### Description

The [hibernate-orm 6.0 migration guide](https://github.com/hibernate/hibernate-orm/blob/6.0/migration-guide.adoc#instant-mapping-changes) states the following in regards to some backwards incompatible instant mapping changes:

> To retain backwards compatibility, configure the setting `hibernate.type.preferred_instant_jdbc_type` to `TIMESTAMP`.

This property is not exposed in quarkus, currently requiring you to configure it like this:

> quarkus.hibernate-orm.unsupported-properties."hibernate.type.preferred_instant_jdbc_type"=TIMESTAMP

I suggest adding this and other properties mentioned in the migration guide (e.g. `preferred_duration_jdbc_type`) to quarkus.

### Implementation ideas

Also consider `hibernate.type.prefer_native_enum_types`

👉 Ai là khách hàng mục tiêu? Họ thuộc nhóm nào?

👉 Vấn đề nào đang giải quyết? Mang lại giá trị gì nổi bật?

👉 Các loại chi phí chính là gì?

issues.title: For self-hosted instances, do not redirect to ente.io
Allow ARM deployments to specify additional parameters
issues.body:
Currently all ARM deployment parameters are inferred from settings retrieved from environment configuration, however, there are scenarios where this isn't flexible enough.  For example:

* A parameter value that can be derived from another configuration source
* A parameter value that is deployment-specific rather than environment specific (e.g. the version of a container image to be used)

The proposal is to extend the schema used by the `RequiredArmDeployments` configuration property to allow additional parameters to be specified.

### Description

When an inline editable node is selected in the guest frame, the InlineToolbar jumps to the far left, if the selected element has a small width:

issues.title: Performance issue related to BitFieldCoder::get
issues.body:
As reported by Nicolas Morange:  

All calls related to getting the position of a cell use a DDSegmentation::BitFieldCoder object.  The problem is, the function used absolutely everywhere is this one: `long64 get(long64 bitfield, const std::string& name) const` which does a `std::map::find(name) `instead of retrieving the index only once and using l`ong64 get(long64 bitfield, size_t idx) const` As this behaviour is in many very basic classes in `DD4Hep::DDSegmentation` and in `FCCDetectors::DetSegmentation`, it is used in many hot loops, and so this std::map::find amounts to 15% of the total CPU spent in my jobs...  A priori the fix is simple, i.e get the indices from the strings in the initialization of the algorithms/tools, and then use the correct function.

![Screenshot_20220629_181656(1)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5057884/176841046-d8dca72e-c5a0-4ab6-b67f-fc23ef740755.png)

issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I had searched in the [issues](https://github.com/apache/doris/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and found no similar issues.


### Description

Doris have add a new datatype about binary,
And now need support some binary functions.
some function have implement for string type in Doris, so need explands it for varbinary type.
and those function could ref [velox ](https://facebookincubator.github.io/velox/functions/presto/binary.html) or [doris](https://doris.apache.org/zh-CN/docs/dev/sql-manual/sql-functions/scalar-functions/string-functions) 。

if you wants implement one of function as below, you could comment and pick it like [issue](https://github.com/apache/doris/issues/48203)，
and when you implement the function, you maybe could refer [this](https://github.com/apache/doris/issues/48201) to know what you should do.


```
1. length(varbinary) -> int
2. md5(varbinary) -> string
3. sm3(varbinary) -> string
4. xxhash_32(varbinary) -> int
5. xxhash_64(varbinary) -> bigint
6. sha1(varbinary) -> string

issues.title: chore: add security scanner to PR builder for NPM audit log
issues.body:
### Current Limitation

Currently, there is no automated security scanning integrated into the PR builder workflow to audit dependencies for vulnerabilities using `npm audit`. This leads to:

- Potential introduction of vulnerable dependencies into the codebase
- Lack of visibility into security risks before merging PRs
- Manual effort required to check audit results for each PR
- Delayed detection of critical/high vulnerabilities
- Inconsistent adoption of security best practices across contributors

Without automated security scanning, the codebase may contain:

- Outdated or vulnerable npm packages
- Security issues that could be caught earlier in the development lifecycle
- Lack of transparency for reviewers and contributors regarding dependency health

### Suggested Improvement

Integrate an automated security scanner into the PR builder workflow to run `npm audit` for every pull request. The scanner should generate an audit log as a build artifact or post a summary to the PR.

## Implementation Plan

1. Update the CI/CD workflow (GitHub Actions) to run `npm audit` on all PRs.
2. Store the audit results as an artifact or comment a summary on the PR.
3. Configure the workflow to fail the build if critical/high vulnerabilities are detected, or warn as per project policy.
4. Document the new workflow in the repository's `CONTRIBUTING.md` or CI documentation.

**References:**
- [npm audit documentation](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v7/commands/npm-audit)
- [GitHub Actions: Uploading build artifacts](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/storing-workflow-data-as-artifacts)
- [Example: npm audit GitHub Action](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/npm-audit-action)

### Please select the package issue is related to

@asgardeo/javascript, @asgardeo/browser, @asgardeo/nextjs, @asgardeo/react, @asgardeo/vue

Current

issues.title: [Bindings] Generate TypeScript Bindings for Limited Time Drop Contract
issues.body:
### 🎯 Objective
Generate TypeScript bindings for the **Limited Time Drop Contract** to manage time-sensitive product drops and access control with type safety.

---

### 🏗 Implementation Steps

**1. Contract Deployment**
```bash
stellar contract upload \
    --source-account <identity or secret key> \
    --network testnet \
    --wasm ./target/wasm32v1-none/release/limited_time_drop.wasm

stellar contract deploy \
    --source-account <identity or secret key> \
    --network testnet \
    --wasm-hash <wasm_hash_from_install_step>
```

**2. Generate TypeScript Bindings**
```bash
stellar contract bindings typescript \
    --network testnet \
    --id <contract_address_from_deploy_step> \
    --output-dir ./packages/limited_time_drop \
    --overwrite
```

**3. Build and Integrate**
```bash
cd packages/limited_time_drop
npm install
npm run build
cd ../..

npm add file:./packages/limited_time_drop
```

**4. Create Contract Client**
```typescript
// src/lib/contracts/limited_time_drop.ts
import * as Client from "limited_time_drop";
import { PUBLIC_STELLAR_RPC_URL } from "$env/static/public";

export default new Client.Client({
  ...Client.networks.testnet,
  rpcUrl: PUBLIC_STELLAR_RPC_URL,
});
```

---

### 🗂 Expected Bindings Structure
```typescript
// Drop management functions
- create_drop(config: DropConfig): u32
- get_drop(drop_id: u32): Drop
- update_drop(drop_id: u32, updates: DropUpdates): void
- cancel_drop(drop_id: u32): void
- check_access(drop_id: u32, user: Address): bool
- grant_access(drop_id: u32, user: Address): void
- revoke_access(drop_id: u32, user: Address): void
- participate_in_drop(drop_id: u32): void
- get_drop_status(drop_id: u32): DropStatus
```

---

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Contract deployed and bindings generated
- [ ] Drop management functions typed
- [ ] Access control functions available
- [ ] Time-based operations supported
- [ ] Contract client integrated

---

We might need to explicitly request the framerate when selecting a webcam, and the default resolution should be the biggest one that has a framerate at lest greater than 30 - [ ] When deleting a node between 2 nodes, the app should automatically check if the path can be instead reconnected so that the 1st node is connected to the 3rd node instead of both nodes being disconnected. - [ ] Node menus should have the option for a user to easily "move" the input link of a node to another one, where for example the user moves his cursor to the input of the node accepting an output from a previous, and where that input is there is some sort of small icon which the user can click on and it will disconnect the previous node from the current one while keeping the link connected to the user's cursor allowing him to connect it instead to a different node. Or a keyboard shortcut (like pressing SHIFT) to avoid cluttering the UI. - [ ] There should be a keybind which easily allows the user to insert or disconnect a node between 2 nodes, where for example he could hold Shift and if the mouse cursor is over a specific node path, the node can be inserted between them. I think we can even do something like in Blender with the Node Wrangler addon, where just drag'n'dropping a node onto a link inserts it. - [ ] Button to "mute" a node, turning it into just a reroute node between its first input and its first output. This allows to quickly enable / disable a node to see what impact it has on the visuals - [ ] Allow controlling every mark of the gradient (position and color) from the graph, even adding / removing marks. (This should probably be done in the scripting graph. The most common use case is to use some Midi to control it, so it's okay for a scripting graph, we don't necessarily want to change it differently on every pixel based on a 2D map) - [ ] Use Variables everywhere, so we can have Metadatas, history, etc. - [ ] Audio window - [ ] In input number, allow to input expressions like `2+3` (which will be evaluated to 5) (support some constants like PI) - [ ] When drag-n-dropping an image or video inside Coollab, automatically create an Image / Video node - [ ] Shortcut to reset a value to the default: - [ ] Double-click on the name (like DaVince Resolve) - [ ] Backspace as in Blender ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a500c950-828b-47df-b567-89062e0669c7) - [ ] When a Point2D is outside of the View, we should clamp it to the border so that it is still accessible. (maybe also a shortcut like CTRL+click to teleport it to where we click ? Or a way to copy the coordinates of the point that we clicked on the view (like a right-click menu?)) - [ ] Customizable keyboard shortcuts (https://youtu.be/9tWEsqIgeDY?t=264) - [ ] "Random" node whose value changes each time we reset the time (see https://discord.com/channels/846087110758891540/1374734924854333491) ## Not so important - [ ] Instead of autosaving every 5 seconds, add an option to autosave anytime we make a change (e.g. anytime there is a new entry in the history) - [ ] Replace ImGui's "Dock Menu" (the ugly arrow button that I removed) by a context menu on right-click on the tab / window title bar? Because we sometimes still need its content, e.g. to hide titlebar on timeline window if we accidentaly show it - [ ] If a user clicks too fast with right mouse button, the menu for Nodes won't appear. - [ ] Option to save the layout of all imgui windows, and then restore it. By default there would be the default layout saved, which allows you to restore it. - [ ] "Init Particles Count" doesn't have a menu appear if you right click on the Particles Count to reset the value back to default - [ ] In notifications, if there is just one word which is very very very long the window will expand to infinity - [ ] App logo doesn't have higher resolution icons for taskbar when scaled on Linux ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33732521-5507-480b-907d-fc75f4494dc6) - [ ] Crash when exporting an image that is too big (e.g. 100000x1000000) - [ ] When clicking in a drag number input, and then clicking on the nodes workspace window, the cursor is teleported back to the number input - [ ] When increasing ui zoom and then putting it back to normal it adds a big padding on the right of the nodes (which is gone when we restart the app). Probably something caused by the fact that the library stores the Bounding Box of the node, and it knows how to expand it if we need more space, but does never shrink it back if we don't need that space anymore. We have the same problem if we change the style options to add some spacing, and then reset the style options - [ ] Launcher: ENTER shortcut to create a new project - [ ] Launcher: CTRL+R to select recent projects, and when releasing CTRL we open that project - [ ] Launcher: List of versions is rarely needed - [ ] Launcher: Collapse title bars "Projects" - [ ] Launcher: Folder where projects will be saved should be a small button somewhere? - [ ] programaticcally force size and position of timeline window to make sure its visible even on smaller screen / differenty UI scale - [ ] alt + enter to toggle fullscreen - [ ] "main node" -> "active view" / "active output" - [ ] hover on a pin -> tooltip that says you can alt + click to remove - [ ] on video node, ui that show where we are in the timeline of the video

issues.title: Secondary User Store Test Connection Fails on Retry After a Previous Failure, Even with Correct Configurations
issues.body:
### Description

When editing a secondary user store, if a Test Connection attempt fails, and the configurations are subsequently corrected, a retry still results in a failure—even though the configuration is valid. However, when the page is navigated away from and then revisited, the connection appears successful.

🔎 This issue is observed only when editing an existing secondary user store. It does not occur when adding a new secondary user store.

Upon inspection, it was identified that after the initial failure, the second Test Connection request sends an empty string for the connectionPassword, rather than reusing the previously provided encrypted password.

A screen recording demonstrating this behavior can be found below: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bdbc736c-d853-450d-bb4a-e07e166598d1

📤 Request Comparison

Property | Initial Successful Request | Second Request After Failure -- | -- | -- connectionPassword | "ENCRYPTED PROPERTY" | "" (empty string) connectionURL | "jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/patch-4044-shared-db?useSSL=false" | "jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/patch-4044-shared-db?useSSL=false" domain | "test" | "test" driverName | "com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver" | "com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver" username | "root" | "root" > ⚠️ **Note:** Ideally, the `connectionURL` should not contain `useSSL=false`. This is a known issue tracked under [#24533](https://github.com/wso2/product-is/issues/24533).

⚠️ Observed Behavior

After a failed attempt, the password is not retained. The system sends an empty string in the next request, resulting in a connection failure—even if the other configuration properties are correct.

This happens even when the “Update connection password” checkbox is not selected, which implies the password should remain unchanged.

✅ Expected Behavior

If the “Update connection password” checkbox is not selected, the previously entered encrypted password should be retained and sent in subsequent requests—unless explicitly changed by the user. Sending an empty password should be avoided unless the user clears the field manually.

### Steps to Reproduce 1. Edit an existing secondary user store. 2. Try a **valid configuration** and click **Test Connection** → observe that the connection **succeeds**. * Inspect the network request and verify that the `connectionPassword` field contains `"ENCRYPTED PROPERTY"`. 3. Now update the configuration to be **intentionally incorrect** (e.g., invalid hostname or port) and click **Test Connection** → observe that the connection **fails**. 4. Correct the configuration back to valid values **without modifying the password**. 5. Click **Test Connection** again → observe that the test **still fails**, even though the configuration is correct. * Inspect the network request again and note that the `connectionPassword` field now contains `""` (empty string). 6. Navigate to another tab and return → observe that the connection shows as **successful**, confirming that the corrected configuration was indeed valid. 📹 *Refer to the attached video above for a full demonstration.* ### Please select the area issue is related to User & Identity Administration ### Version wso2is-7.2.0-m6-SNAPSHOT ### Environment Details (with versions) N/A ### Developer Checklist - [ ] [Behavioural Change] Does this change introduce a behavioral change to the product? - [ ]  ↳ Approved by team lead - [ ]  ↳ Label `impact/behavioral-change` added - [ ] [Migration Impact] Does this change have a migration impact? - [ ]  ↳ Migration label added (e.g., `7.2.0-migration`) - [ ]  ↳ Migration issues created and linked - [ ] [New Configuration] Does this change introduce a new configuration? - [ ]  ↳ Label `config` added - [ ]  ↳ Configuration is properly documented

issues.title: Merge tt_version and semver_t
issues.body:
## Overview

We have two structures representing semantic versioning of different components (KMD, firmware etc...). They both have (major, minor, patch) semantics of semantic versioning https://semver.org/.

There is an opportunity to merge these two structures and use the merged structure in all places where versioning is needed.

## Current implementation

There are 2 structures for versioning

- https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-umd/blob/main/device/api/umd/device/utils/semver.hpp

- https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-umd/blob/main/device/api/umd/device/types/cluster_types.hpp#L187

Both are used in the code in different places. 

## Requested change

Requested change is to keep only one of these structures. `semver_t` looks like more complete structure at the moment so it would be easier to keep that one. If any of the features of  `tt_version` are ported to `semver_t` as well, we would like to see added tests in https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-umd/blob/main/tests/misc/test_semver.cpp or any similar file that becomes test file for the versioning structure.

## Definition of done

Only one structure for semantic versioning exists. That one is used in UMD code whenever we want to keep track of semantic versioning.

## Additional notes

Comparing firmware versions in UMD code is not the same as comparing other versions.

Rules for comparing firmware

- Major version 80 is older than major version 18
- Minor versions are compared regularly
- Patch versions are compared regularly

Other versions follow the regular comparing of semantic versions (first major, then minor, then patch)

issues.title: chore: set up `Storybook` for Component Library Documentation and Testing
issues.body:
### Current Limitation

Currently, the `@asgardeo/react` UI components doesn't have support for testing in isolation. This creates several development and testing challenges:

**Current State:**
- No **Storybook** visual component documentation or testing platform
- Components like `OrganizationSwitcher`, `CreateOrganization`, etc. can only be tested within full application context
- Difficult to test component variations, edge cases, and different prop combinations in isolation
- No **Storybook** stories to showcase component API and usage examples
- Manual testing required for UI regression detection without **Storybook** visual testing

**Missing Storybook Capabilities:**
- Interactive **Storybook** component playground for developers
- **Storybook** visual regression testing for UI components
- **Storybook** component documentation with live examples
- Isolated testing environment for different component states
- **Storybook** design system validation and consistency checking
- **Storybook** accessibility testing in isolation

### Suggested Improvement

Implement **Storybook** for component testing in isolation across the React packages in the monorepo.

1. Install Storybook Dependencies
- Install Storybook core packages and React framework support in the monorepo root
- Add Storybook addons for accessibility testing, essentials, and visual regression testing

2. Add Storybook to `@asgardeo/react` Package
- Configure Storybook to target the React components in the `@asgardeo/react` package
- Set up Storybook to discover and load stories from the React package components
- Configure Vite framework integration for optimal build performance

3. Add Storybook to `@asgardeo/nextjs` Package  
- Extend Storybook configuration to include Next.js specific components
- Configure story discovery for Next.js package components
- Ensure compatibility with Next.js component patterns

4. Create Storybook Stories Structure
- Add `.stories.tsx` files alongside existing components like `OrganizationSwitcher`
- Create stories for different component states (default, loading, error)
- Document component props and usage examples in stories

5. Integrate with Existing i18n System
- Configure Storybook to use the existing translation system from `packages/javascript/src/i18n/`
- Set up locale switching in Storybook toolbar using the `en-US` translations
- Enable testing components in different language contexts

6. Configure Storybook Addons
- Set up accessibility addon for WCAG compliance testing
- Configure visual regression testing with Chromatic
- Add design tokens addon for consistent theming
- Enable essential addons for controls, docs, and viewport testing

7. Add Build Scripts
- Add Storybook development and build scripts to package.json
- Configure Storybook build output for deployment
- Set up Storybook static build generation

issues.title: feat: add `WCAG 2.2` Compliance and Accessibility Testing to `@asgardeo/react` & `@asgardeo/nextjs` UI Components
issues.body:
### Current Limitation

The `@asgardeo/react` & `@asgardeo/nextjs` UI components lack comprehensive accessibility features and WCAG 2.2 compliance:

**WCAG 2.2 Compliance Issues:**
- Missing support for new WCAG 2.2 success criteria (Focus Appearance, Dragging Movements, Target Size)
- Non-compliant focus indicators and target sizes
- Lack of proper keyboard navigation patterns

**Keyboard Navigation Issues:**
- Organization switcher dropdown cannot be navigated with keyboard
- Modals lack proper focus management and keyboard shortcuts
- No Escape/Enter key handling

**ARIA Support Gaps:**
- Missing ARIA labels for interactive elements
- Dropdown menus lack aria-expanded, aria-haspopup attributes
- Modal dialogs missing aria-modal, aria-labelledby
- No screen reader announcements for organization switches

**Focus Management:**
- Modals don't trap focus
- Focus not restored when modals close
- Missing visual focus indicators that meet WCAG 2.2 standards

**Testing:**
- No automated WCAG 2.2 accessibility testing
- Missing keyboard navigation tests
- No screen reader compatibility verification

### Suggested Improvement

Add comprehensive WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility support with proper testing:

## Implementation Areas

### 1. WCAG 2.2 Compliance
- **Focus Appearance (2.4.11)**: Enhanced focus indicators with proper contrast
- **Target Size (2.5.8)**: Ensure interactive elements meet 24x24px minimum
- **Dragging Movements (2.5.7)**: Provide keyboard alternatives for any drag interactions
- **Fixed Reference Points (2.4.12)**: Consistent navigation patterns

### 2. ARIA Enhancements
- Add proper ARIA attributes to dropdowns and modals
- Implement live regions for dynamic announcements
- Add descriptive labels for all interactive elements

### 3. Keyboard Navigation
- Arrow keys for dropdown navigation
- Enter/Space for selection, Escape to close
- Focus trapping in modals with Tab/Shift+Tab
- Focus restoration when closing modals

### 4. Screen Reader Support
- Live announcements for organization switches
- Loading state announcements
- Error message announcements

### 5. Custom Accessibility Hooks
```tsx
// WCAG 2.2 compliant hooks
useFocusTrap(isActive: boolean)
useFocusRestore()
useAnnouncement()
useKeyboardNavigation()
useWCAGCompliantFocus()
```

### 6. Testing with Vitest + WCAG 2.2
```tsx
// WCAG 2.2 automated testing
test('meets WCAG 2.2 AA standards', async () => {
  // axe-core with WCAG 2.2 rules
});

// Focus appearance testing
test('focus indicators meet WCAG 2.2 standards', () => {
  // Focus visibility and contrast testing
});

// Target size validation
test('interactive elements meet 24x24px minimum', () => {
  // Target size compliance testing
});
```

## Benefits
- **WCAG 2.2 AA compliance** for legal requirements
- **Enhanced focus indicators** for better visibility
- **Improved target sizes** for touch and motor accessibility
- **Better keyboard-only navigation**
- **Screen reader compatibility**
- **Automated accessibility regression prevention**

## Key Files to Update
- OrganizationSwitcher components (ARIA + keyboard + WCAG 2.2)
- Modal components (focus management + target sizes)
- New accessibility hooks with WCAG 2.2 compliance
- CSS for WCAG 2.2 compliant focus indicators
- Vitest setup for axe-core with WCAG 2.2 rules
- ESLint jsx-a11y rules updated for WCAG 2.2

issues.title: [Bindings] Generate TypeScript Bindings for Referral Contract
issues.body:
## 🎯 Objective
Generate TypeScript bindings for the **Referral Contract** to provide type-safe referral program management, level tracking, and reward distribution operations.

---

### 🏗 Implementation Steps

**1. Contract Deployment**
```bash
stellar contract upload \
    --source-account <identity or secret key> \
    --network testnet \
    --wasm ./target/wasm32v1-none/release/referral_contract.wasm

stellar contract deploy \
    --source-account <identity or secret key> \
    --network testnet \
    --wasm-hash <wasm_hash_from_install_step>
```

**2. Generate TypeScript Bindings**
```bash
stellar contract bindings typescript \
    --network testnet \
    --id <contract_address_from_deploy_step> \
    --output-dir ./packages/referral_contract \
    --overwrite
```

**3. Build and Integrate**
```bash
cd packages/referral_contract
npm install
npm run build
cd ../..

npm install file:./packages/referral_contract
```

**4. Create Contract Client**
```typescript
// src/lib/contracts/referral_contract.ts
import * as Client from "referral_contract";
import { PUBLIC_STELLAR_RPC_URL } from "$env/static/public";

export default new Client.Client({
  ...Client.networks.testnet,
  rpcUrl: PUBLIC_STELLAR_RPC_URL,
});
```

---

### 🗂 Expected Bindings Structure
```typescript
// Admin functions
- initialize_referral_contract(admin: Address): void
- update_admin(new_admin: Address): void
- pause_contract(): void
- resume_contract(): void

// Referral management
- register_referral(referrer: Address, referee: Address): void
- get_referral_team(referrer: Address): Vec<Address>
- get_referral_level(referrer: Address): u32
- update_team_size(referrer: Address, new_size: u32): void

// Level management
- get_level_requirements(level: u32): LevelRequirements
- check_level_progression(referrer: Address): bool
- get_user_level(referrer: Address): u32

// Rewards management
- calculate_reward(referrer: Address, amount: u64): u64
- distribute_reward(referrer: Address, amount: u64): void
- get_milestone_rewards(referrer: Address): Vec<MilestoneReward>
- claim_milestone_reward(referrer: Address, milestone_id: u32): void

// Verification
- verify_referral(referrer: Address, referee: Address): bool
- get_verification_status(referrer: Address): VerificationStatus
```

---

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Contract deployed and bindings generated
- [ ] Referral management functions typed
- [ ] Level progression functions available
- [ ] Reward distribution included
- [ ] Verification system supported

issues.title: [data grid] Adding two rows when using row spanning does not work when grid is first empty
Implement controllable temporal height
issues.body:
Enable a user to be able to adjust the temporal height of a block. This height represents the number of rounds of stabilizer measurement. 

A memory experiment typically needs d rounds. Subtracting one layer for initialization and another for measurement, we get d-2 rounds of memory. In `tqec` we parameterize circuits by k (defined in section VIII of [the review paper](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1gCNpSdvE7Xtnf6Onh05vz9PX_WkjNv2r/view?pli=1)) such that d=2k+1. The `start_simulation_using_sinter` method allows users to specify a range of values for k to generate circuits that scale with the code distance. In the case of this Issue, we want to keep the spatial code distance fixed and only increase along the time axis. 

Additional details and some ways this could be useful are discussed [here](https://github.com/tqec/tqec/issues/533#issuecomment-2787759680). We don't expect programs which control k to be an integral part of the tool's usage, but the flexibility could be useful for certain users, and refactoring the code to support it could be a good exercise for those interested.
