issues.title: 🏷️[Deprecate]: outdated functionality before v3
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Some functionality is already rather old and has increasing technical debt. We should make sure that we start building a newer secret store approach (see #438 ) that is prepared for the future. **Describe the solution you'd like** First step is to deprecate the following services:

Arcus.Security.Core

 * [ ] `CachedSecretProvider` ➡️ we will configure caching on the secret store itself. #456 * [ ] `CacheConfiguration` ➡️ we don't need additional classes to configure a single value (cache duration) right now. #456 * [ ] `ICacheConfiguration` ➡️ we don't need additional interfaces for classes to configure a single value (cache duration) right now. #456 * [ ] `ICachedSecretProvider` ➡️ we will configure caching on the secret store itself, instead of having multiple cached versions on each secret provider. #456 * [ ] `SecretProviderCachingExtensions` ➡️ we will configure caching on the secret store itself, which makes extensions like these unnecessary. #456 * [ ] `CriticalExceptionFilter` ➡️ once we have a new interface that allows secret provider implementations to respond with a secret result (success/failure) there is no need for additional functionality like this on the secret store to pass additional information on 'why' a certain secret provider failed, as all the failed reasons will be aggregated in a single result. * [ ] `ISecretProviderExtensions` ➡️ any extensions here will become unnecessary once we have the new `ISecretProvider` interface. * [ ] `.AddEnvironmentVariables(...)` ➡️ both extensions will become unnecessary in favor of a new set with and without `Action` options. * [ ] `.AddConfiguration(...)` ➡️ both extensions will become unnecessary in favor of a new set with and without `Action` options. * [x] `ISecretProvider` ➡️ we will create a new interface without the 'raw secrets' and with a 'sync' variant instead, in the `Arcus.Security` namespace. (#450) * [ ] `ISecretStore` ➡️ we will create a new interface implementing the new `ISecretProvider` interface with just a single member `TProvider GetProvider(string name) where TProvider : ISecretProvider` in the `Arcus.Security` namespace instead. #456 * [ ] `ISyncSecretProvider` ➡️ we will have a new `ISecretProvider` interface that already has the synchronous variant. * [ ] `IVersionedSecretProvider` ➡️ we will stop supporting 'versioned secrets' as something that every secret provider could support, and instead provide members on concrete secret provider implementations (currently only Azure Key Vault supports versioned secrets in our setup). * [ ] `MutatedSecretNameCachedSecretProvider` ➡️ we will run the secret name mutation in the secret store itself before contacting the secret provider, instead of having a dedicated class for this. #456 * [ ] `MutatedSecretNameSecretProvider` ➡️ we will run the secret name mutation in the secret store itself before contacting the secret provider, instead of having a dedicated class for this. * [ ] `Secret` ➡️ we will work with a `SecretResult` instead that the secret providers return, that contains the name/value/version of the secret. * [ ] `SecretNotFoundException` ➡️ we will work with a `SecretResult` isntead that the secret providers return, that contains the name/value/version of the secret. * [ ] `SecretProviderOptions` ➡️ we will work with a new set of options that only has `string ProviderName` and `.MapSecretName(Func mapper)` members in the `Arcus.Security` namespace. (#451) * [ ] `SecretStoreAuditingOptions` ➡️ we will remove the hard link with Arcus Observability. * [ ] `SecretStoreBuilder` * [ ] `.SecretStoreSources` ➡️ we will not expose the secret sources this way, but rather register them in the service collection instead. * [ ] `.CriticalExceptionFilters` ➡️ once we have a new interface that allows secret providers to respond with a secret result (success/failure) there is no need for additional functionality lie this on the secret store to pass additional information on 'why' a certain secret provider failed, as all the failed reasons will be aggregated in a single result. * [ ] `.AddProvider(ISecretProvider)` ➡️ will be replaced by an overload with the new interface. * [ ] `.AddProvider(ISecretProvider, Action)` ➡️ will be replaced by an overload with the new interface/options. * [ ] `.AddProvider(Func, Action)` ➡️ will be replaced by an overload with the new interface/options. * [ ] `.AddCriticalException(...) (2) ➡️ new functionality has secret result which has no need for 'critical exceptions' to pass additional information on 'why' a certain secret provider failed to retrieve the secret. * [ ] `SecretStoreSource` ➡️ will be replaced by a new `internal` registration class for the new interface. (#452) #456

Arcus.Security.Providers.AzureKeyVault

 * [ ] `ArcusConfigurationProvider` ➡️ old class that initially was to add secrets back to the app configuration setup. * [ ] `IKeyVaultConfiguration` ➡️ interface not needed for configuring a single value (vault URI). * [ ] `KeyVaultConfiguration` ➡️ class not needed for configuring a single value (vault URI). * [ ] `KeyVaultOptions` ➡️ we remove the hard link with Arcus Observability, which was the only reason why have this options model. * [ ] `.AddAzureKeyVault(...)` extensions ➡️ all current extensions are obsolete in favor of consolidating the different authentication mechanisms #456 * [ ] `KeyVaultCachedSecretProvider` ➡️ caching will be handled on the secret store itself. #456 * [ ] `KeyVaultSecretProvider` constructors (2) ➡️ we will pass in the `SecretClient` itself in an internal constructor instead, so that people can use the Azure SDK registered clients for it. * [ ] `.Logger` ➡️ we will stop supporting inheriting secret providers in such a way. * [ ] `.Get(Raw)Secret(Async)` ➡️ we will use the new interface to retrieve secrets. * [ ] `.StoreSecretAsync` ➡️ we will use a new member `.SetSecretAsync` that returns a secret result instead. * [ ] `.GetSecretClient` ➡️ we will stop supporting inheriting secret providers in such a way.

Arcus.Security.Providers.CommandLine

 * [ ] `CommandLineSecretProvider` constructor ➡️ will be replaced by a constructor that has also the `SecretProviderOptions`. * [ ] `.Get(Raw)Secret(Async)` ➡️ will be replaced with the new secret provider interface. * [ ] `SecretStoreBuilderExtensions.AddCommandLine(string[] args, string name, ...)` ➡️ will be replaced by an overload that takes in the `Action` instead.

Arcus.Security.Providers.DockerSecrets

 * [ ] `DockerSecretsSecretProvider` constructor ➡️ will be replaced by a private constructor and factory method that builds the `KeyPerFileConfigurationProvider` instead and with the new `SecretProviderOptions` model. * [ ] `Get(Raw)Secret(Async)` ➡️ will be replaced with the new secret provider interface. * [ ] `SecretStoreBuilderExtensions.AddDockerSecrets(..., Func...)` (2) ➡️ will be replaced with an overload with `Action` instead.

✔️ Arcus.Security.Providers.HashiCorp

 * [x] `HashiCorpVaultOptions.TrackDependency` ➡️ hard link with Arcus Observability will be removed. * [x] `HashiCorpVaultUserPassOptions` ➡️ we will not provide extension overloads for different authentication types, so we don't need this options model anymore. * [x] `SecretStoreBuilderExtensions` * [x] `.AddHashiCorpVaultWithUserPass` (3) ➡️ we will not provide extension overloads for different authentication types in favor of passing the `VaultSettings` directly. * [x] `.AddHashiCorpVaultWithKubernetes` (2) ➡️ we will not provide extension overloads for different authentication types in favor of passing the `VaultSettings` directly. * [x] `.AddHashiCorpVault(Func)` ➡️ we will provide an overload with a new `Action` overload, which removes the need for complex members like these. * [x] `.AddHashiCorpVault(...)` (2) ➡️ we stop supporting inheriting secret providers in such a way. * [x] `HashiCorpSecretProvider` * [x] `.GetTrackedSecretAsync` ➡️ we remove the hard link with Arcus Observability plus removing the inheriting support * [x] `.Get(Raw)Secret(Async)` ➡️ we will use the new secret provider interface instead.

✔️ Arcus.Security.Providers.UserSecrets

 * [x] `SecretStoreBuilderExtensions` * [x] `.AddUserSecrets(...Func)` (6) ➡️ we will use a new overload with the new options `Action` instead. * [x] `UserSecretsSecretProvider` * [x] constructor ➡️ will be replaced by private constructor and internal factory method that creates the `JsonConfigurationProvider` instead. * [x] `.Get(Raw)Secret(Async)` ➡️ will be replaced by new secret provider interface instead.
**Additional context** See #438 for background inforation.

issues.title: [FEATURE] : [STAX] Add Integrity Check Support for Authorize, PSync, Refund and RSync Flows
issues.body:
### Feature Description/Summary

Integrity check is a scenario where there is a discrepancy between the amount sent in the request and the amount received from the connector, which is checked during response handling.

### Context
Integrity checks in a payments flow are critical for ensuring data consistency, correctness, and security when dealing with amounts between Hyperswitch and connectors like Adyen, Stripe, Razorpay, etc.

### Starter Tasks

- In the `handle_response` function of Authorize/PSync/Refund/RSync, you will have to call the respective functions - `get_authorise_integrity_object` for Authorize, `get_sync_integrity_object` for Payments Sync, `get_refund_integrity_object` for Refund and RSync and `get_capture_integrity_object` for Capture. 
- You would have to call these functions from `crates/hyperswitch_connectors/src/utils.rs`.
- These functions expect `amount_convertor`, `amount` and `currency`.
- You can take a look at this [PR](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/pull/8075) for reference.

### Implementation Hints

- You can go to `crates/hyperswitch_connectors/src/connectors/stax.rs` and call the respective integrity check function as stated above in the `handle_response` function

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Request and Response body added for each of the flows where integrity check is applied.
- [ ] All the required GitHub checks passing
- [ ] Formatted the code using `cargo +nightly fmt --all`

### How to Test it 

- Hardcode the amount or currency field that is being passed to the connector different from the one you are passing in the request body
- This way you would be able to reproduce the integrity checks error message while testing.

### Mentor Contact

- Tag @bsayak03 [Sayak Bhattacharya] in the comments if you have any doubts/queries

issues.title: [REFACTOR]: Relocation tool call and reasoning parser to the same location
issues.body:
### Feature request

Both tool calling parsing and reasoning parsing share the same idea that they both parse the model output and extract out related content into a structured field in response. So conceptually the invocations should happen in the same location, however, currently the two parsers happen in different locations:

- Reasoning parser: in [delta.rs](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/delta.rs#L374-L382)
- Tool calling parser: in [preprocessor.rs](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs#L983-L988)

Initial discussion with @ayushag-nv that relocating tool calling parser to within delta.rs gives better flexibility as the message in delta.rs contains both text and token so the parser can consume either depending on the need and efficiency. Whereas in preprocessor, the only option is to parse based on text.

issues.title: MCP Integration System
issues.body:
# MCP Integration System Implementation Plan

## Overview

Implement a comprehensive Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration system for Inbox Zero AI that allows users to connect external services (HubSpot, Monday.com, Salesforce, Notion, etc.) and have AI agents automatically use these tools to enhance email responses and automation.

## Key Architecture Principles

- **Use Existing MCP Servers**: Leverage official MCP servers provided by services (e.g., HubSpot's `https://mcp.hubspot.com/`, Monday.com's `@mondaydotcomorg/monday-api-mcp`)
- **AI-Native Tool Discovery**: AI agents can discover and call MCP tools directly via `tools/list` and `tools/call`
- **User-Controlled Access**: Users control which MCP servers are connected and which tools are approved for AI usage
- **Secure Credential Management**: All credentials are encrypted and isolated per user/organization
- **Organization Support**: Team-wide integrations where appropriate

---

## Stage 1: Database Schema & Core Infrastructure

**Objective**: Extend database schema to support MCP integrations and connection management.

**Location**: 
- `apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma`
- New migration files

**Database Models**:
```sql
-- Available MCP integrations catalog
model McpIntegration {
  id          String @id @default(cuid())
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
  
  name        String @unique  // "hubspot", "monday", "salesforce"
  displayName String          // "HubSpot CRM"
  description String?
  
  // Connection details
  serverUrl   String?         // For remote servers like HubSpot
  npmPackage  String?         // For npm package servers like Monday
  authType    String          // "oauth", "api-token", "basic"
  
  // Configuration
  defaultScopes String[]      // Default OAuth scopes
  isActive      Boolean @default(true)
  
  connections McpConnection[]
}

-- User/organization connections to MCP servers
model McpConnection {
  id          String @id @default(cuid())
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
  
  // Relationships
  integrationId String
  integration   McpIntegration @relation(fields: [integrationId], references: [id])
  
  // Owner (user-level or org-level)
  userId         String?
  user           User? @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  organizationId String?
  organization   Organization? @relation(fields: [organizationId], references: [id])
  
  // Connection details
  name           String          // User-friendly name
  isActive       Boolean @default(true)
  
  // Encrypted credentials
  accessToken    String?         // Encrypted OAuth token
  refreshToken   String?         // Encrypted refresh token
  apiKey         String?         // Encrypted API key
  expiresAt      DateTime?
  
  // Approved scopes/tools
  approvedScopes String[]
  approvedTools  String[]        // Specific tool names approved for AI usage
  
  tools McpTool[]
  
  @@unique([userId, integrationId])
  @@unique([organizationId, integrationId])
}

-- Track available and enabled tools per connection
model McpTool {
  id           String @id @default(cuid())
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt
  
  connectionId String
  connection   McpConnection @relation(fields: [connectionId], references: [id])
  
  name         String         // Tool name from MCP server
  title        String?        // Human-readable title
  description  String?        // Tool description
  schema       Json?          // Input schema
  
  isEnabled    Boolean @default(true)  // User can disable specific tools
  
  @@unique([connectionId, name])
}
```

**Actions**:
1. Add new models to Prisma schema
2. Create database migration
3. Update Prisma client
4. Add necessary indexes for performance

---

## Stage 2: MCP Server Registry & Discovery

**Objective**: Create a registry of available MCP servers and connection management system.

**Location**: 
- `apps/web/utils/mcp/registry.ts`
- `apps/web/utils/mcp/connection-manager.ts`

**MCP Server Registry**:
```typescript
export const MCP_INTEGRATIONS = {
  hubspot: {
    name: "hubspot",
    displayName: "HubSpot CRM",
    description: "Access HubSpot CRM data for contacts, deals, and companies",
    serverUrl: "https://mcp.hubspot.com/",
    authType: "oauth",
    defaultScopes: [
      "crm.objects.contacts.read",
      "crm.objects.companies.read", 
      "crm.objects.deals.read"
    ],
    oauthConfig: {
      authUrl: "https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize",
      tokenUrl: "https://api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token",
      userLevel: true // Requires user-level installation
    }
  },
  monday: {
    name: "monday",
    displayName: "Monday.com",
    description: "Create and manage Monday.com boards and items",
    npmPackage: "@mondaydotcomorg/monday-api-mcp",
    authType: "api-token",
    defaultScopes: []
  },
  // ... other integrations
} as const;
```

**Actions**:
1. Create MCP integration registry with connection details
2. Build MCP connection manager for OAuth flows
3. Implement credential encryption/decryption utilities
4. Add connection health monitoring and token refresh
5. Create API routes for connection management

---

## Stage 3: Authentication & Security Layer

**Objective**: Implement secure credential storage and OAuth flows for MCP integrations.

**Location**:
- `apps/web/app/api/mcp/` (new API routes)
- `apps/web/utils/mcp/auth.ts`

**API Routes**:
- `POST /api/mcp/connect` - Initiate connection to MCP server
- `GET /api/mcp/oauth/callback` - Handle OAuth callbacks
- `DELETE /api/mcp/disconnect` - Remove MCP connection
- `GET /api/mcp/connections` - List user's MCP connections
- `POST /api/mcp/tools/sync` - Sync available tools from MCP server

**Security Features**:
- All credentials encrypted using existing `encryptToken`/`decryptToken` utilities
- Per-user credential isolation
- Organization-level vs user-level connection logic
- OAuth 2.1 support with PKCE for future compatibility
- Automatic token refresh handling

**Actions**:
1. Create OAuth flow handlers for each supported service
2. Implement secure credential storage using existing encryption
3. Add API routes for MCP connection management
4. Create middleware for validating MCP access permissions
5. Add organization-level connection support

---

## Stage 4: MCP Orchestration Layer

**Objective**: Create system to route MCP requests to appropriate servers with user credentials.

**Location**:
- `apps/web/utils/mcp/orchestrator.ts`
- `apps/web/utils/mcp/client.ts`

**MCP Orchestrator Responsibilities**:
1. **Tool Discovery**: Call `tools/list` on connected MCP servers
2. **Tool Execution**: Route `tools/call` requests to appropriate servers
3. **Credential Injection**: Attach user credentials to MCP requests
4. **Error Handling**: Handle connection failures and token refresh
5. **Permission Checking**: Ensure user has approved tool usage

**Example Usage**:
```typescript
const orchestrator = new McpOrchestrator(userId);
const availableTools = await orchestrator.listTools();
const result = await orchestrator.callTool("get_contact_details", { email: "user@example.com" });
```

**Actions**:
1. Build MCP client wrapper for HTTP and npm package servers
2. Implement tool discovery and caching
3. Create request routing logic based on tool names
4. Add comprehensive error handling and retries
5. Implement tool permission checking

---

## Stage 5: AI Integration Points

**Objective**: Integrate MCP tools into existing AI workflows for email drafting and automation.

**Location**:
- `apps/web/utils/ai/mcp-tools.ts`
- `apps/web/utils/reply-tracker/generate-draft.ts` (enhance)

**AI Integration Features**:
- **Context Gathering**: Query CRM for contact/company information before drafting
- **Dynamic Tool Selection**: AI decides which tools to use based on email context
- **Fallback Handling**: Graceful degradation when MCP tools fail
- **Prompt Enhancement**: Include MCP tool results in AI prompts

**Example AI Workflow**:
1. User receives email from potential customer
2. AI identifies sender email and company
3. AI calls HubSpot MCP tools to get contact/deal information
4. AI uses CRM context to draft personalized response
5. AI can also update CRM with interaction notes

**Actions**:
1. Modify AI drafting system to include MCP tool discovery
2. Add context gathering from external systems
3. Implement intelligent tool selection logic
4. Add error handling and fallbacks for MCP failures
5. Create prompt templates that effectively use MCP context

---

## Stage 6: User Interface & Configuration

**Objective**: Create UI for users to manage MCP integrations and configure tool usage.

**Location**:
- `apps/web/app/(app)/[emailAccountId]/integrations/` (new pages)
- `apps/web/components/integrations/` (new components)

**UI Components**:
- **Integrations Dashboard**: Overview of connected services
- **Connection Flow**: OAuth and API key setup wizards  
- **Tool Configuration**: Enable/disable specific MCP tools
- **Usage Analytics**: Show MCP tool usage statistics
- **Error Monitoring**: Display connection issues and resolution steps

**Pages**:
- `/integrations` - Main integrations dashboard
- `/integrations/connect/[integration]` - Connection setup flow
- `/integrations/[connectionId]/configure` - Tool configuration
- `/integrations/[connectionId]/usage` - Usage analytics

**Actions**:
1. Create integrations management dashboard
2. Build connection setup flows for each service type
3. Add tool configuration interface with granular controls
4. Create connection status monitoring and error reporting
5. Add usage analytics and audit logging

---

## Stage 7: Organization-Level Features

**Objective**: Implement organization-wide MCP integrations for team collaboration.

**Location**:
- `apps/web/app/(app)/[emailAccountId]/organization/integrations/` (new)
- Extend existing organization management

**Organization Features**:
- **Shared Connections**: CRM access shared across team members
- **Permission Management**: Control who can configure org integrations
- **Usage Policies**: Set rules for AI tool usage across organization
- **Audit Logging**: Track integration usage across team
- **Billing Integration**: Usage-based billing for organization integrations

**Actions**:
1. Add organization-level MCP connection support
2. Implement permission system for integration management
3. Create shared vs personal integration logic
4. Add billing considerations for organization usage
5. Implement comprehensive audit logging

---

## Stage 8: Testing & Documentation

**Objective**: Comprehensive testing and documentation for production readiness.

**Location**:
- `apps/web/__tests__/mcp/` (new test directory)
- Documentation in existing docs structure

**Testing Coverage**:
- Unit tests for MCP utilities and orchestration
- Integration tests for OAuth flows and API connections
- End-to-end tests for AI tool usage workflows
- Load testing for MCP server connections
- Security testing for credential handling

**Documentation**:
- User guides for setting up integrations
- Developer documentation for adding new MCP servers
- API documentation for MCP endpoints
- Troubleshooting guides for common issues

**Actions**:
1. Write comprehensive unit and integration tests
2. Add end-to-end tests for complete user workflows
3. Create user documentation for integration setup
4. Write developer guides for extending the system
5. Add monitoring and alerting for production deployment

---

## Success Metrics

- **User Adoption**: 70% of active users connect at least one MCP integration
- **AI Enhancement**: 80% improvement in email response relevance when MCP context is available
- **Tool Usage**: Average of 5+ MCP tool calls per AI-generated email draft
- **Reliability**: 99.5% uptime for MCP integration functionality
- **Security**: Zero credential leakage incidents

## Risk Mitigation

- **Start Small**: Begin with HubSpot integration as proof of concept
- **Graceful Degradation**: AI works without MCP tools when connections fail
- **Security First**: Use existing encryption patterns and security reviews
- **Rate Limiting**: Implement proper rate limiting for external API calls
- **Monitoring**: Comprehensive logging and alerting for integration health

## Technical Dependencies

- Existing authentication system (better-auth)
- Current encryption utilities (`encryptToken`/`decryptToken`)
- Organization management system
- AI/LLM integration infrastructure
- Prisma database management

This plan leverages existing MCP servers from major providers while creating a robust orchestration layer that allows AI agents to seamlessly use external tools to enhance email automation and responses.

## UPDATE: Recommended MCP Packages Structure

### **`packages/mcp/`** (Single Package)
```
packages/mcp/
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts           # Main exports
│   ├── orchestrator.ts    # MCP orchestration logic
│   ├── integrations.ts    # Integration registry
│   ├── client.ts          # Custom MCP client wrapper
│   └── types.ts           # TypeScript types
├── package.json
└── README.md
```

Following the pattern of `packages/loops/`, this would be a single, focused package that handles all MCP-related functionality.

## Benefits of Package Approach

1. **Separation of Concerns**: MCP logic isolated from main web app
2. **Reusability**: Could be used by other apps (like the unsubscriber)
3. **Community Contributions**: Easier for contributors to add new integrations
4. **Testing**: Isolated testing of MCP functionality
5. **Versioning**: Independent versioning of MCP features

## Recommendation

Start with a single **`packages/mcp/`** package that contains:
- MCP orchestration logic
- Integration registry
- Custom client wrapper
- TypeScript types

This follows the existing pattern and keeps it simple while providing all the benefits of the package structure.

issues.title: [Feature] Add FreeBSD support for process monitoring in procmond component
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

Home labs and small businesses often use **pfSense** and **OPNsense** routers/firewalls, which are based on FreeBSD. Currently, DaemonEye has no planned support for FreeBSD-based systems, limiting its usefulness for monitoring these critical network infrastructure components.

## Proposed Solution

Implement basic FreeBSD support in the **procmond** component by leveraging existing capabilities:

### Technical Approach

1. **Leverage sysinfo crate**: The `sysinfo` crate already provides cross-platform system information gathering with FreeBSD support
2. **Extend platform detection**: Add FreeBSD target detection using `cfg(target_os = "freebsd")` conditionals
3. **Process monitoring foundation**: Build upon existing process monitoring patterns used for Linux/Windows

### Implementation Plan

#### Phase 1: Basic Process Monitoring
- [ ] Add FreeBSD target configuration in procmond Cargo.toml
- [ ] Implement FreeBSD-specific process enumeration using sysinfo
- [ ] Add basic process metrics collection (CPU, memory, PID)
- [ ] Test on FreeBSD 13.x/14.x systems

#### Phase 2: Enhanced Capabilities
- [ ] Explore FreeBSD-specific crates for advanced monitoring:
  - `freebsd` crate for system calls
  - `kvm` bindings for kernel virtual memory access
- [ ] Add network interface monitoring
- [ ] Implement system resource monitoring

#### Phase 3: pfSense/OPNsense Optimization
- [ ] Test specifically on pfSense and OPNsense systems
- [ ] Add firewall-specific monitoring capabilities
- [ ] Document deployment procedures for FreeBSD-based routers

## Use Cases

- **Router Monitoring**: Monitor pfSense/OPNsense router performance and processes
- **Firewall Health**: Track critical firewall services and resource usage  
- **Network Infrastructure**: Comprehensive monitoring of FreeBSD-based network appliances
- **Home Lab Environments**: Support for popular open-source router/firewall platforms

## Technical Considerations

- **Dependency Compatibility**: Verify all current dependencies support FreeBSD
- **Testing Environment**: Need access to FreeBSD test systems
- **Documentation**: Update installation and configuration docs for FreeBSD

## Alternative Solutions

1. **Container-based approach**: Run DaemonEye in a FreeBSD jail
2. **Remote monitoring**: Use existing Linux/Windows agents with remote FreeBSD monitoring
3. **Third-party integration**: Integrate with existing FreeBSD monitoring tools

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] procmond component compiles and runs on FreeBSD 13.x+
- [ ] Basic process monitoring functionality works on FreeBSD
- [ ] Successfully tested on pfSense and/or OPNsense systems  
- [ ] Documentation updated with FreeBSD deployment instructions
- [ ] CI pipeline includes FreeBSD compatibility checks (if possible)

## Implementation Notes

- Start with the sysinfo crate's existing FreeBSD support
- Consider FreeBSD version compatibility (minimum supported version)
- Plan for testing on actual pfSense/OPNsense hardware or VMs

## Contribution

- [x] I'm willing to help implement this feature
- [x] I can help with testing this feature  
- [x] I can help with documentation
- [x] I can provide feedback during development

issues.title: Project Idea Submission & Voting System 💌
issues.body:
Add Idea Submission Features on the 👇🏻 https://www.devdisplay.org/IdeaSubmission

# **Description** Add the Project Idea Submission and Voting System to DevDisplay can make it a hub for innovation and collaboration. This feature allows users to submit ideas, vote on their favorites, and actively participate in bringing top-voted ideas to life through collaborative development. Here's a detailed overview of the feature, enhanced with functionalities to ensure engagement and utility. --- ## **Feature Workflow Overview** 1. **Idea Submission Window (First Week of Every Month):** - Allow users to submit their project ideas within the first week of every month. - Display a countdown timer on the homepage indicating the time left to submit ideas. - Ideas are displayed publicly for voting immediately after submission. 2. **Voting Phase (Throughout the Month):** - Users can like or upvote their favorite ideas to boost their ranking. - A **"Trending Now" Section** highlights the top-voted ideas dynamically. 3. **End-of-Month Selection (Final Week):** - At the end of the month, the top **1 most-voted idea** is selected for community implementation. - Recognize contributors with badges like **"Innovator of the Month"** for the selected idea. 4. **Community Collaboration (Next Month):** - The selected idea is moved to a **“Project Development Hub”** where the community collaborates to implement it. - Users can join specific tasks like design, development, testing, or documentation. --- ## **Detailed Features** ### **1. Idea Submission** - **Submission Form:** - **Title:** A short, engaging title for the idea. - **Description:** Provide details about the project, its purpose, and potential use cases. - **Tags:** Keywords for categorization (e.g., #AI, #Frontend, #OpenSource). - **Resources Needed:** Option to list the skills or tools required for implementation. - **Optional Media Uploads:** Attach images, mockups, or concept diagrams. - **Validation:** Ensure users can only submit one idea per month. ### **2. Voting System** - **Likes and Upvotes:** - Each idea has a like button and an upvote counter displayed prominently. - Limit each user to one vote per idea to ensure fair participation. - **Real-Time Leaderboard:** - Display top 5 trending ideas on the homepage dynamically. - Add a **"Voting Closes In"** timer to create urgency for participation. ### **3. Collaboration Hub for Top Ideas** Once an idea is selected: - **Task Board:** Break the project into smaller tasks (design, code, testing, etc.) and allow users to claim tasks based on their expertise. - **Role-Based Contributions:** Assign roles like Project Lead, Developer, Designer, Tester, etc., to contributors. - **Community Chatroom:** Add a real-time chat or discussion board for seamless collaboration. - **Progress Tracker:** Use a Kanban-style board to show progress and keep the community updated. ### **4. Rewards & Recognition** - **Innovator of the Month:** Recognize the user whose idea is selected with a badge and showcase them on the homepage. - **Contributor Highlights:** Display names of all contributors to the implemented project. - **Portfolio Integration:** Allow contributors to link their involvement to their profiles as achievements. ### **5. User-Friendly Discovery** - **Browse Ideas by Category:** Filter ideas by tags or categories (e.g., Web Development, Machine Learning). - **Search and Sort:** Allow sorting by trending, newest, or highest-voted ideas. - **Idea History:** Maintain an archive of past submitted ideas for inspiration. ### **6. Notifications** - Notify users about: - The start of the submission phase. - Voting deadlines and reminders. - Announcement of the selected idea. - Updates about the implementation phase. --- ## **Benefits for the Community** 1. **Encourages Innovation:** - Opens up a platform for users to pitch and develop creative ideas. 2. **Crowdsourced Validation:** - Community voting ensures the best ideas rise to the top. 3. **Skill Building:** - Participants gain hands-on experience in collaborative development. 4. **Community Recognition:** - Motivates users with badges, leaderboard rankings, and project credits. 5. **Stronger Collaboration:** - Encourages teamwork within the community, fostering connections and learning opportunities. --- ### 📬 Want to contribute? Comment below to get assigned! If you're picking this up, make sure to follow the contribution guidelines in the repository. **💡 Before diving in, make sure to:** ✅ Add your profile to DevDisplay. ⭐ Star the repository to show your support and stay updated with new features! **🚨 This is the first & mandatory step in becoming a contributor.** --- #### **For More Details and Help** - **Join DevDisplay Discord Community**: [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/chyt2UgTv5) - Connect with other developers and collaborate on exciting projects. - **Reach Out to the Team**: - Company Email: team@devdisplay.org - Creator's Email: hellow.ashutosh@gmail.com - **Connect on Social Media**: - **GitHub Organization**: https://github.com/devdisplay - **LinkedIn**: https://www.linkedin.com/company/devdisplay/ - **Twitter**: https://x.com/devdisplay_ - **Instagram**: https://www.instagram.com/devdisplay/ --- ### **Thanks and Best Regards** The **DevDisplay Team** 💌 ---

issues.title: Add Google OAuth Login to Shopiko
issues.body:
Currently, Shopiko allows users to sign up and log in using traditional email + password authentication. While this works well, many users today prefer a quicker, password-free experience using their Google account.

Let’s enhance Shopiko’s login system by integrating Google OAuth (Firebase/Auth0/Passport.js OAuth strategy). This will make signing in faster, more secure, and user-friendly — reducing friction for first-time users.

Why this is needed?
Improves user experience with one-click login.
Increases trust since Google login feels safer for many users.
Saves time — no need to remember another password.

What needs to be done?
Set up Google OAuth (using Passport.js or Firebase).
Add a “Login with Google” button on the login/register page.
Ensure OAuth users can still use cart, orders, and checkout seamlessly.
Store OAuth user data securely in MongoDB.
(Optional) Allow linking Google account with existing Shopiko account.

Expected Outcome
Users can log in either via Email/Password (existing) OR Google (new).
Cart, checkout, and order history should work smoothly for OAuth users too.
Clean UI integration for the Google login button.
Tech Reference
Passport.js Google OAuth Docs
Firebase Authentication Google Sign-in

Difficulty Level 🟠 Medium
